articles.title: Josh Allen contra todos
articles.standfirst: Para Luckia es el principal favorito de ser el MVP de la temporada regular de la NFL
articles.summary: Para Luckia es el principal favorito de ser el MVP de la temporada regular de la NFL
articles.body: La NFL vuelve a rugir esta madrugada del jueves y, como cada año, el debate por el MVP de la temporada regular ya calienta las casas de apuestas antes de que se juegue un solo down. La lista está dominada, una vez más, por quarterbacks, y el mercado deja ver una carrera apretada en la zona alta, aunque con un nombre que se despega ligeramente del resto. Ese nombre es Josh Allen, favorito a cuota 6 en Luckia. El de los Buffalo Bills llega respaldado por tres temporadas seguidas superando las 4.000 yardas totales y por un perfil de doble amenaza —brazo y piernas— que los votantes han premiado en el pasado. Buffalo está entre los conjuntos con mejores opciones de terminar arriba en la AFC, y esa combinación de producción individual y éxito colectivo es exactamente la fórmula que históricamente decide este premio. Allen no necesita una temporada perfecta para meterse en la conversación: le basta con ser el motor de un equipo contendiente. Pisándole los talones aparece Lamar Jackson, a cuota 9. El de los Baltimore Ravens llega con el aval de haber ganado el galardón en dos ocasiones y con Baltimore instalado, como de costumbre, entre los aspirantes al mejor récord de la conferencia. El principal interrogante es la salud: una 2025 marcada por las lesiones le impidió pelear el trofeo de tú a tú, y su cuota refleja tanto su techo altísimo como la cautela lógica tras un año interrumpido. Detrás de los dos favoritos, el mercado de apuestas deportivas en Luckia agrupa a una terna de mariscales de campo, los tres a cuota 10. Justin Herbert llega con un argumento reforzado. Recupera a sus dos tackles All-Pro y suma a Mike McDaniel como coordinador ofensivo, dos piezas que pueden destrabar el techo que Los Angeles Chargers no habían terminado de explotar. Drake Maye, por su parte, llega de protagonizar la pelea por el MVP más cerrada del año pasado, cuando terminó como subcampeón de la votación tras liderar a New England hasta una consistente campaña y una carrera en playoffs; si los Patriots vuelven a mandar en el Este de la AFC, Maye entra de lleno en la discusión. Completa el trío Joe Burrow, que pese a sus números de élite nunca ha recibido un solo voto de primer lugar para el MVP, en buena medida por los problemas físicos que le han costado seis o más partidos en tres de sus seis temporadas como profesional; cuando ha estado sano, sin embargo, su producción por partido ha estado entre las mejores de la liga, y eso explica por qué su cuota ha ido apretándose en las últimas semanas. Un peldaño más abajo asoma Patrick Mahomes, a cuota 12. El de Kansas City Chiefs sigue siendo, casi por definición, parte de cualquier conversación de MVP cuando su equipo compite arriba en la AFC, pero llega condicionado por la rotura de ligamento cruzado que sufrió al final de la temporada pasada. Su cuota, más alta de lo habitual en él, es en realidad un reflejo directo de esa incertidumbre física antes de que arranque la campaña. Cierra el quinteto principal Matthew Stafford, el vigente ganador del premio, a cuota 13. La historia reciente del galardón juega en su contra. Las repeticiones consecutivas son la excepción, no la norma, y el mercado está fijando ese precio incluso para un quarterback que llega de conquistar el MVP tras una gran temporada con Los Angeles Rams. Defender el trono siempre es la misión más difícil en la NFL, y las casas de apuestas ya lo están descontando.

articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Los Angeles Rams y San Francisco 49ers en el Melbourne Cricket Ground correspondiente a la primera semana de la NFL
articles.body: Los Angeles Rams y San Francisco 49ers abren la temporada 2026 de la NFL este jueves en un escenario totalmente inédito. El Melbourne Cricket Ground, en Australia, acogerá por primera vez en la historia un partido de temporada regular de la liga. El choque, correspondiente a la Semana 1, se disputará en la madrugada de este viernes para el horario español, con un componente añadido de incertidumbre por el particular calendario de viajes al que se enfrentan ambos equipos antes del estreno. Favorito para el partido entre Rams y 49ers Los Rams llegan a este duelo tras protagonizar, junto a los 49ers, una de las temporadas más históricas de la NFC West. Ambos equipos terminaron la pasada campaña con récord de 12-5, ganaron sus respectivos partidos de Wild Card, y solo cayeron ya en instancias mayores, los Rams en la final de conferencia ante los Seahawks y los 49ers en la ronda divisional. El conjunto de Sean McVay, con Matthew Stafford como gran referencia tras su candidatura al MVP, parte esta temporada con el objetivo de dar el salto definitivo hacia la Super Bowl. Por su parte, los 49ers afrontan el arranque con Christian McCaffrey como principal arma ofensiva y con la incorporación de Mike Evans en el receptor. Kyle Shanahan buscará además corregir el punto más débil de su defensa el curso pasado, con apenas 20 capturas de mariscal de campo, la cifra más baja de toda la liga. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito a Los Angeles Rams. 1XBET paga la victoria angelina a cuota 1.46, por 2.72 la victoria del cuadro de la bahía. Hándicap de puntos El mercado de hándicap aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. Los Rams llegan con una defensa reforzada en la línea de presión y con Stafford en un gran momento de forma, mientras que los 49ers arrastran dudas sobre su capacidad para generar presión sobre el mariscal rival tras su pobre registro de capturas la temporada pasada. Con estos datos , el hándicap de -3.5 puntos a favor de Los Angeles luce como un mercado con valor en las apuestas deportivas. 1XBET paga esta opción a cuota 1.82, por 1.98 del caso contrario. Total de puntos (Over/Under) El mercado de puntos totales apunta hacia un partido con bastante producción ofensiva por ambos lados. Tanto Stafford como McCaffrey se mostraron entre los jugadores más determinantes de la pasada temporada regular, y ambos ataques suelen generar puntos con facilidad incluso ante defensas de nivel. Con estos datos, 1XBET sitúa la cuota del +48.5 puntos totales a 1.90, por 1.90 del caso contrario. Total de touchdowns L.A Rams(Over/Under) El mercado de touchdowns de L.A Rams se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. Los de Sean McVay cuentan con un ataque de gran calidad, apoyados en jugadores como Puka Nacua o Kyren Williams, lo que invita a pensar en un partido con anotaciones frecuentes desde el primer cuarto. 1XBET paga el +3.5 touchdowns del equipo angelino a 2.5, por 1.53 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Trinity Rodman isn't skipping her Spirit match to watch the U.S. Open final. Why would she?
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman won't miss this weekend's crucial Washington Spirit match against the Boston Legacy. She isn't skipping a game that holds implications for fir...
articles.body:
Trinity Rodman won't miss this weekend's crucial Washington Spirit match against the Boston Legacy.

She isn't skipping a game that holds implications for first place in the NWSL to attend the U.S. Open men's singles tennis final — potentially featuring her boyfriend, Ben Shelton, who took defending champion Carlos Alcaraz to five sets and a tiebreak in the wee hours of Wednesday morning.

That doesn't mean she's unwilling to support Shelton in a relationship that has become increasingly buzz-worthy since the pair went public in March 2025 — it's simply a reflection of how both balance their relationship alongside their demanding schedules. Still, it is Rodman who faces a disproportionate amount of questions about her ability to do both.

Rodman was at Arthur Ashe Stadium at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center late Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, just days after assisting the Spirit's winning goal against the Thorns in Portland. Still awake for Shelton's final ace at 3:33 a.m., she celebrated with his signature "dialed in" phone celebration. She was also visibly miffed as Shelton joked about his best friend and sister needing to work in three hours and hoping they could get the day off. The cameras caught her with her arms out as she said, "What about me?"

The Spirit confirmed seven hours later that she'd be in uniform on Sunday, and that she was at the team's training facility in Virginia, reporting at 9 on Wednesday morning. Rodman even shared the video for proof.

She's also not the only one committing to intense travel at all hours to show up as part of this athlete power couple. The support goes both ways .

Shelton has popped up at Spirit games after quick turnarounds, most notably last November after his first appearance in the ATP finals.

On Nov. 14, he lost to Jannik Sinner in Turin, Italy, in straight sets, starting at 2 p.m. local. By 12 p.m. ET the next day, he was at the Spirit's semifinal win over the Portland Thorns in a field-level suite at Audi Field to watch Rodman. The following week, he made the trip to San Jose to support his girlfriend and the Spirit at the NWSL Championship. The gesture was largely seen in a positive light.

"Some people can say that it's difficult to maintain a relationship where you have two professional athletes," Shelton recently told the ATP Tour. "But in my opinion, to have somebody who understands what you go through is very, very important."

Rodman was able to use a long injury layoff to attend multiple tournaments for Shelton last year, but not without scrutiny.

"Yes, I'm grinding almost every day in PT to get back on the field," she wrote on a social media post in May 2025, pushing back on the narrative that she couldn't show up for her partner and work on her personal recovery goals. "NO, I'm not just being a wag and vacationing:) thank you."

WAG, short for wives and girlfriends, was coined by British tabloids as shorthand for footballers' significant others when reporting their every move and look — most notably, Victoria Beckham. The phenomenon has continued to follow players of all sports and their partners.

Rodman has typically embraced playfulness over defensiveness when it comes to her relationship. She has not forgotten who she is in these moments — nor has it deterred her from showing off her unique fashion choices — but has navigated the discourse over their relationship by largely letting it pass her by and staying on her own message.

After all, most of it is not within her control.

She doesn't control ESPN's caption, which described her as "Ben's girlfriend & USWNT player" during Shelton's first-round match last week. She responded at his second-round match , wearing a T-shirt that read "I ❤️ my boyfriend." By then, the order had been reversed following backlash.

Rodman cannot stop ESPN commentators from speculating if she would miss a regular-season match that has the chance to lift her team to No. 1 in the standings to attend the U.S. Open men's final, presuming Shelton gets past Frances Tiafoe in Friday's semifinal match. The chance that tennis commentator John McEnroe knows much about the Spirit beyond Rodman's involvement seems infinitesimal.

This is the friction that keeps popping up and, more often than not, in Rodman's direction rather than Shelton's. It is why there is a defensiveness from others on her behalf; it is far more normal for her own accomplishments and responsibilities to be diminished in favor of Shelton's, or for her to be talked about in relation to other men (either Shelton, or far more frequently, her father despite her own clearly stated wishes for that to end). The Grand Slams element doesn't lessen the attention.

In September 2025, Sheldon was shown on screen during a Spirit game with the title "Trinity Rodman's +1" on a Paramount+ broadcast (a game Rodman scored both goals, helping the Spirit capture a 2-0 win over the Seattle Reign at Audi Field). That one didn't go viral. It was also clearly meant in a playful manner, rather than ESPN's attempt at informing viewers.

The NWSL is happy to draft off Shelton's profile and his relationship with Rodman, both in their quest for new fans and as the league sees Rodman as one of the primary breakthrough stars of American women's soccer. But the NWSL ecosystem centers on Rodman, not Shelton.

For years, we have seen World Cup winners described in headlines as someone's wife. It's not just a women's soccer problem. Watch any USA Hockey broadcast during the Olympics, and husbands and fathers are talked about nearly as much as the action on the ice. There's a clear pattern across sports media as a whole.

Rodman's chosen approach resists that history. She even embraces the term WAG. When speaking with Kylie Kelce on her "Not Gonna Lie" podcast, Rodman said she doesn't mind the word choice because it simplifies what she's choosing to do when she shows up to support Shelton.

Despite her disinterest in engaging, despite her consistently choosing to opt for playfulness rather than being defensive, it doesn't mean she enjoys it at the end of the day.

"It's a blessing in so many ways," Rodman told Kelce on being in a relationship that had captured the public's attention, before agreeing with Kelce's interjection that it was also "garbage."

"Too many people have too many opinions that they need to speak on," Rodman concluded, "and it's just like, mind your business."

articles.title: Why are Claude Lemieux’s final days drawing attention after brother Jocelyn Lemieux’s emotional revelations about the NHL legend
articles.summary: NHL News: Jocelyn Lemieux reflects on the untimely passing of his brother, NHL star Claude Lemieux, in an emotional interview that reveals family insights and the impact of brain health on former players.
articles.body: The last days of Claude Lemieux are receiving renewed attention after his brother Jocelyn Lemieux spoke about the former NHL star’s death, the family’s grief and the unanswered questions surrounding the tragedy. Jocelyn sat down with Mario Langlois on 98.5 FM’s Les amateurs de sports in his first major interview since the death of his brother in May 2026.The timing has made the tragedy especially difficult for the hockey world. Days before his death, Claude Lemieux was at the Bell Center, carrying the torch before a Montreal Canadiens playoff game. He was 60 years old and had a celebrated NHL career that included four Stanley Cup championships. did Jocelyn Lemieux reveal about Claude Lemieux’s final days?It’s still pretty fresh for them, Jocelyn Lemieux said. His brother was doing fine and then all of a sudden he was gone. We’re still trying to get our heads around it. In the interview, Jocelyn said he had stopped trying to understand exactly what happened, adding that some questions may never have clear answers.Claude Lemieux’s last public appearance was May 25, when he carried the torch at Bell Center during the Eastern Conference Final featuring the Montreal Canadiens. His death just days later is a painful juxtaposition and has been difficult to process for family members and the broader NHL community.The timing was especially shocking, Jocelyn said, because the brothers had been together and, from his perspective, Claude appeared to be relaxed. The revelation has added emotional context to what was a shocking event for former teammates, NHL organisations and fans.What did Jocelyn Lemieux say about family letters?Jocelyn said Claude Lemieux also left letters to family members before his death. The messages have given relatives another personal connection to the former Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche star during a particularly difficult time.Earlier reports also described messages left by Claude for loved ones. But the family's discussion has been less about the sensational details, and more about the emotional weight of discovering a side of Claude that his brother said he hadn't really known.Jocelyn Lemieux has been open about his own history with concussions and the potential long-term effects of repeated head trauma. Questions have also been raised about Claude’s brain health, as his family announced that Claude’s brain would be donated to Boston University’s CTE Center for research. Before making any diagnosis, a scientific analysis should be done.The issue adds another layer to the larger NHL conversation involving player health, brain injuries and life after hockey. In a career that lasted from 1983-2009, Claude Lemieux was known for a very physical and competitive style of play.His legacy is still defined by his major postseason performances, including Stanley Cup championships with the Montreal Canadiens in 1986, the New Jersey Devils in 1995 and 2000 and the Colorado Avalanche in 1996. He also captured the Conn Smythe Trophy with New Jersey in 1995.Jocelyn said the family would continue to honour his brother. articles.title: Angel Reese Drops Caitlin Clark Truth Bomb After Team USA Win
articles.summary: Once again, Team USA delivered a dominant World Cup performance, blowing out Hungary 108-56 on Thursday morning.Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier led the...
articles.body:
Once again, Team USA delivered a dominant World Cup performance, blowing out Hungary 108-56 on Thursday morning.

Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier led the charge for Team USA with 19 points in 15 minutes of play. It was two other WNBA stars off the bench, though, who flexed their muscles when they were together on the court.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese dominated Hungary in her 18 minutes on the court with 9 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals, and 1 block. Reese's teammate, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark , had a pretty good day herself with 10 points, 9 assists, 3 rebounds, and 2 steals in the win. Clark and Reese, though, had everyone noticing the chemistry they share.

Angel Reese & Caitlin Clark Dominate Together in Team USA Win

Throughout the game, Clark connected with Reese on multiple passes that resulted in a score. Reese also helped out on the boards to support Clark and the offense on missed shots.

After the game, Reese was asked about the chemistry that she and Clark have built during the World Cup. Reese was honest about how well the two have worked together.

"I'm sure we know each other's game like the back of each other's hand … So it's fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're going to be USA teammates for a while."

Reese and Clark have been playing off the bench the whole tournament so far. Clark is leading the team in assists, and Reese is top three in rebounds on Team USA.

Team USA Advances in World Cup Thanks to Caitlin Clark & Angel Reese

Reese has been dominant on defense all World Cup long, matching how she has played in the WNBA this season. The same could be said about Clark with her three-point shooting and passing.

Team USA is lucky to have two of the best players in the world on the same team. While some question why both are playing off the bench, the strategy has clearly worked, as Clark and Reese are playing good basketball.

Team USA will have a short break before the semifinals, and they'll need their stars off the bench to keep playing well. Reese and Clark will play major roles for Team USA as they go for the gold.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Sleepers, Week 1: If you just lost Brock Bowers, his teammate can help fill the void
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski reveals six players who could help fantasy managers with surprise performances in Week 1.
articles.body:
It's a new year and the sleeper page is back in action, a weekly look at under-rostered players who can help your fantasy team win (or perhaps fill a DFS spot). Keep an open mind and do some digging with us.

Some standard caveats come into play for Week 1 sleepers. Your fantasy roster will never be as healthy as it is right now, and we're a solid month away from bye weeks. If there's ever a time to be playing the hits, rolling with your primary players, it's right now. But shrewd fantasy managers are always on the lookout for undervalued players and depth additions, so let's make sure we keep our focus.

Raiders TE Michael Mayer vs. Dolphins (11% rostered)

It was a gut punch to hear the Brock Bowers injury news this week; he underwent meniscus trim surgery Tuesday and will miss 1-2 games . But don't overlook the talented Mayer, who was a second-round pick three years ago after a strong career at Notre Dame (he's the most productive receiving tight end in Notre Dame history). Mayer's best NFL start wasn't long ago — a snappy 8-89-0 run against the Giants last December — and Kirk Cousins often locks in on his tight ends. Miami was very poor in tight end coverage last year .

Shough made a lot of believers with his finishing kick last year, giving us a solid six-pack of starts to end the season (QB12, QB6, QB16, QB16, QB9, QB4). Head coach Kellen Moore is a creative schemer who runs his offense at a faster tempo, which helps the volume. Shough is working with decent pass-catchers (WR Chris Olave is a star, TE Juwan Johnson forever underrated) and the matchup should present points; the game total is posted at 50.5 (highest on the slate) and the Lions won't have impact safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph for at least a month. Let's play some pinball in Detroit .

The Texans acquired veteran David Montgomery and immediately installed him as their starting running back, but the team realizes that Montgomery — entering his age-29 season — probably needs a proactive running mate. Marks was a mild disappointment as a rookie, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry and getting limited receiving use, but he was a busy receiver in college (261 receptions over five seasons) and the Texans were expanding his route tree this summer. Keep an eye on him.

Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell vs. Cardinals (41%)

Mitchell's sleeper case had stops and starts all summer — new OC Mike McDaniel pounded the table for Mitchell as a free-agent pickup, but Mitchell dealt with a hamstring injury in August. Omarion Hampton looms as the obvious priority back in Los Angeles , but Mitchell could percolate into a meaty role that equals regular flex consideration. If Mitchell is healthy enough to play Sunday, game script should be his friend — the Chargers are 9.5-point favorites over the hapless Cardinals. If nothing else, Mitchell deserves roster consideration as a one-injury-away upside player.

Raiders WR Tre Tucker vs. Dolphins (31%)

Although Mayer is the cleanest beneficiary to the Bowers injury news, let's also leave the light on for Tucker, ostensibly the No. 1 wide receiver in Las Vegas . Offensive wizard Klint Kubiak immediately makes this offense more interesting, and Tucker is taking aim at a Miami secondary that could be the worst in football.

The nasty Houston defense is probably the best in football, and the Texans had an eight-sack party against Buffalo last November, prompting a 23-19 upset. But Shakir was a slot machine in that game (8-110-0), and although the Bills added D.J. Moore to be their top target for 2026, Shakir still has a reasonable path to 70 or more receptions.

articles.title: ‘My Name Is Julian. I Play Sports’: Meet Ohio State’s Unassuming Superstar QB
articles.summary: Julian Sayin is one of college football’s biggest stars, but the Ohio State QB carries himself like just any other college kid.
articles.body: Julian Sayin’s family group chat was blowing up. A video of Sayin went viral after one of his classmates recorded him introducing himself during the discussion portion of an online sports marketing class in the first week of school. The students had been asked to share their wellness habits. Instead of identifying himself as Ohio State’s starting quarterback or a Heisman Trophy candidate, Sayin kept it as low-key as possible. He tried to be a normal college student. "My name is Julian Sayin, I just prefer Julian," he began. "My major is sport industry. I wouldn’t really say I want to change too much about my physical activity — I feel like I have a pretty good routine, I’m pretty active, I play sports. And one interesting thing about me is I love to play golf and I love playing pickleball." The video spread quickly across social media, in part because of how casual Julian was, but his family wasn’t surprised by it. "It’s very Julian," his older brother, Aidan Sayin, told me with a chuckle. "He’s not going to give you much detail, but just be humble and to the point. We all had a good laugh. "The ‘I prefer Julian’ line was hilarious, but that’s just him. We joke that [his humor is] similar to Larry David. We always watch ‘Curb Your Enthusiasm,’ and say he sort of emulates that same character." Julian’s no-ego personality might be the opposite of what you’d expect from someone at the center of the college football universe. He tries to fly under the radar and never tells anybody who he is if they don’t already know. Fans loved the video and plenty of them flooded the comment section on the social media post. "The video itself encapsulates a lot about him," Aidan said. "He’s not concerned with the spotlight. To be honest, he doesn't even like it. Whenever we're out and about in Columbus, he keeps his hat on, his head down, and just wants to get his açaí bowl." Julian has been that way for as long as those closest to him can remember. It’s part of what makes him so effective on the field. He’ll need to keep that level head as he enters his second season as a starter at Ohio State, where a talent-laden roster is chasing its second national championship in three years. The top-ranked Buckeyes have a challenging schedule ahead with their first major test coming Saturday when they visit Arch Manning and No. 4 Texas in one of the biggest games on the Week 2 slate. 'It Always Came From Within’ Julian is the baby in a family of high achievers. He’s the starting quarterback on the No. 1 team in the country and is a front-runner to win the Heisman after finishing in fourth place last season. But he’s striving to be as accomplished as his three older siblings. "I think he was always kind of scrappy and trying to follow along," Sayin's mom, Karen Brandenburg, told me. "I don’t know how to describe it — it’s kind of like, ‘Don’t think you’re all that.’" Julian’s eldest sister, Bailey, played soccer at the University of Chicago before attending the Cambridge School of Art in England. His sister Jocelyn attended the University of Edinburgh in Scotland, where she earned a degree in data analytics. After returning to the United States, Jocelyn took an interest in her youngest brother’s career, joining him on several college visits to LSU and Ole Miss. Now, alongside their mom, Jocelyn helps manage Julian’s NIL and marketing deals. She also earned a master’s degree in sports management from Ohio State and is pursuing her doctorate. Aidan played football at the University of Pennsylvania, where he graduated with honors from Wharton. He went on to play for the Columbus Aviators of the UFL and is now considering continuing his football career in Japan or Europe. When asked whether the household she and her husband, Dan, created while raising their children influenced their ambition, Brandenburg paused for a moment. She’s Type A; Dan is more laid back. Maybe, she thought, it started with Bailey, who from a young age was determined to play on the best soccer teams. That drive might have trickled down to the rest of the siblings. "I don’t know," Brandenburg said. "But it always came from within. We didn’t have to push. We never had to say, ‘You’ve gotta go to practice.’ They just always sought after things on their own, which made parenting really easy. We’ve been really lucky that they push each other." With success comes praise, and the Sayin kids aren't particularly comfortable with compliments or being celebrated. When Jocelyn was finishing her master’s program, Brandenburg suggested they attend her graduation. Her daughter immediately pushed back: "No, no. When I get my doctorate, we’ll go to graduation." Julian is much the same way. The only feedback he really wants to hear — positive or negative — comes from his coaches and teammates. Even an email from an Ohio State fan in Dayton simply wanting to tell Julian that he had played great didn’t feel right to him. 'On To The Next' Thadd MacNeal — who was both Julian and Aidan’s coach at Carlsbad High School outside of San Diego and is close with the Sayin family — was at Ohio State’s 38-14 win over Penn State last year and sat in on the post-game press conference. He remembers reporters asking Julian about his passing percentage — 87% on a near-perfect 20-of-23 passes — in addition to 316 yards and four touchdowns. "And he literally said, ‘Well, that’s because I have great protection, because my receivers catch every ball, and they’re so productive," MacNeal told me. "It’s always deflecting to other people. That’s just how he operates." When Julian won Elite 11 — a premier high school quarterback competition — in June 2023, his mom wanted to take him out to dinner. He had beaten out Dylan Raiola, the top-rated quarterback recruit in the 2024 class at the time. But Julian declined. There was a tournament about 30 minutes away, and he wanted to go play in it instead. This story came up during one of Julian’s visits to Alabama while he and his family were sitting in Nick Saban’s office. Julian enrolled at Alabama early in January 2024, but on his first day of classes, Saban announced his retirement, prompting the quarterback to enter the transfer portal and head to Columbus. "Nick [Saban] said, ‘Hey, I heard you won Elite 11,’" Brandenburg recalled. "And Julian’s like, ‘Yeah.’ And I said, ‘I tried to take him out to dinner and celebrate.’" "Nick just looked at Julian, and Julian goes, ‘On to the next thing.’ And Nick Saban’s like, 'Yeah, that’s one thing. On to the next.’" That attitude, Brandenburg said, is part of what makes Julian different. "I don’t know what made him that way," Brandenburg added. "But it’s good. It keeps us grounded, too. There’s always the next thing. "I’m really trying to learn from him." ‘Calm And Locked In’ Those traits serve Julian well on the field. He’s calm in big moments and doesn’t let the stage get too big. He’s already off to a fast start this season, completing 21-of-25 passes for 320 yards and three touchdowns before coming out midway through the third quarter in Ohio State’s season-opening 56-3 romp of Ball State. Julian also scored his first rushing touchdown of his collegiate career on a fourth-and-goal to make it 21-0 early in the second quarter. "He seems even more relaxed and confident this year," Brandenburg said. "He’s very calm and locked in." Last year, his first as a starter at Ohio State, Julian completed 77% of his passes and averaged 27.9 attempts per game, the best mark in the country. He threw for 3,610 yards with 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions, leading the Buckeyes to a 12-2 record and impressive wins over Texas and Michigan. They lost to eventual national champion Indiana in the Big Ten title game and runners-up Miami in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal. The year before, Julian played in four games as Will Howard’s backup, completing 5-of-12 passes with one touchdown on an Ohio State team that ultimately won the national championship. Those experiences have helped Julian grow and develop into an even better player. Transforming his body during the offseason, he's stronger, more poised, and Ohio State coach Ryan Day said this summer at Big Ten Media Days that he's carrying himself with "a different look in his eye." Buckeyes center Carson Hinzman has seen it too. "I mean, that dude can roll now," Hinzman told reporters last month. "When he’s talking in the huddle, the confidence he has. Being able to zip that ball, you hear it literally whistle behind your ear, and it gives us confidence to have a quarterback who can go out there and have a little bit of swagger about him." No matter what happens this season — whether Julian wins the Heisman, Ohio State falls to Texas on Saturday or the Buckeyes run the table — his mindset will remain the same. It always has. "I think sometimes bravado or being the star quarterback works, too," Aidan said. "But for the most part, teammates want to see someone who is about the team and isn’t all about themselves. He’s just about playing football. He doesn't care what else goes along with it. He just wants to play football and do his best this week." articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Updates: What We Know About Seahawks QB's Hip Issue
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have reportedly avoided a worst-case scenario with QB Sam Darnold, who suffered a hip injury in Week 1.
articles.body: Seattle Seahawks fans, breathe. While Sam Darnold will likely miss at least one game due to a hip injury he suffered in the team's Wednesday night season opener against the New England Patriots, an MRI has determined that Seattle's starting quarterback "dodged a bullet" and shouldn't miss an extended period of time, NFL Media reported on Thursday afternoon. Darnold hobbled off the field after being sacked on Seattle's opening drive on Wednesday night and didn't return. The Seahawks later announced that Darnold sustained a hip injury and wouldn't return, with backup Drew Lock stepping in and helping Seattle pull off a come-from-behind 13-10 victory over New England. After the game, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald revealed the team was "able to rule out a fracture" regarding Darnold's hip. In what was a rematch of Super Bowl LX, which the Seahawks won 29-13, Lock finished with 187 passing yards, one passing touchdown, no interceptions and a 113.3 passer rating, while completing 72.7% of his passes (16 of 22). If Darnold misses time, Lock would presumably become Seattle's starting quarterback, with second-year signal caller and 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe serving as the backup quarterback. Lock has made 28 starts over his seven-plus-year NFL career (2019-present), most recently making five starts for the New York Giants in 2024. Seattle's next two games are road tilts against the Arizona Cardinals (Sept. 20) and Washington Commanders (Sept. 27). The 29-year-old Darnold is in his second season with the Seahawks. Last year (2025), Darnold earned his second consecutive Pro Bowl nod, throwing for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions, while posting a 99.1 passer rating and completing 67.7% of his passes in a 14-3 season for Seattle.

articles.title: College Football Week 2 Expert Picks, Predictions For Michigan-Oklahoma And More
articles.summary: Here are FOX Sports' expert picks and predictions for Week 2 of the college football season.
articles.body: Will Texas avenge last season's loss to Ohio State? Can Michigan bounce back against Oklahoma after a shocking and controversial near-upset? Which teams will prove that their Week 1 performance wasn't a fluke, but a trend to rely on? The college football season rolls on, and Week 2's lineup is looking strong with some big cross-conference games, from Texas-Ohio State to Michigan-Oklahoma to Illinois-Duke and so many more. So before Week 2 kicks off, we've got some picks of the week, along with answers to those questions and more. We're breaking down our straight-up picks for Week 2 and which matchups to keep a close eye on this weekend. Let's get into it. Kansas vs. No. 23 Missouri When: Friday, 8 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence, KansasLine: Missouri -5.5 RJ Young: MissouriThe Tigers have the better quarterback, and their run game is still rather awesome even without Ahmad Hardy in the backfield. Laken Litman: MissouriMizzou takes down Kansas in an old rivalry game as former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons lights up the Jayhawks with another multi-touchdown performance. Michael Cohen: MissouriAs a new face in a new place, Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons gave the Tigers plenty to be excited about in Week 1 with four touchdowns and only two incompletions. He keeps it rolling against the Jayhawks. Ben Portnoy: MissouriI'm in on Austin Simmons being a difference maker for the Tigers, even with a depleted run game. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz has largely handled business as a favorite during his tenure, and I think he does it again this week. Michigan vs. No. 11 Oklahoma When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX)Where: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MichiganLine: Oklahoma -5.5 Young: Oklahoma The Sooners have the edge at quarterback, wide receiver and defensive line. This could get ugly for Michigan if Bryce Underwood doesn't show a tremendous leap in development. Litman: OklahomaThe biggest question for me is how Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood will look after last week's near disaster against Western Michigan. You know Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables will put together a defensive game plan that makes it as hard as possible for the young signal-caller to succeed. Cohen: OklahomaMaybe the Wolverines will bounce back a bit following last week's controversial win over Western Michigan. But the safer bet is that Oklahoma's terrific defense can cause even more problems for Bryce Underwood, whose time as the starter feels like it's dwindling. Portnoy: OklahomaRecency bias has me incredibly down on the Wolverines, but there's nothing I saw in Saturday's win (?) over Western Michigan that makes me think they can beat a team of Oklahoma's caliber. I think the Sooners are a legit dark horse to win the SEC this year, and I love what a healthy John Mateer brings. Give me the Sooners, big. Oklahoma State vs. No. 6 Oregon When: Saturday, noon ET (ESPN)Where: Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater, OklahomaLine: Oregon -22.5 Young: OregonOregon is coming off of an embarrassing win, still has one of the best rosters in the sport and is about to play an Oklahoma State team that got beat by Tulsa, the smallest FBS school in the country. Name the number, Ducks. Litman: OregonThe Ducks had their "wake-up call" last week vs. Boise State, who could end up being the Group of Six College Football Playoff representative. While Stillwater is a tough place to play, Dan Lanning will have his team ready to go, while the Cowboys are in a transition year. Cohen: OregonThere will certainly be a response from Oregon's defense after the highly-touted unit was gashed by Boise State in a surprisingly close opener. The Ducks should roll against an Oklahoma State team that looked quite rough in an upset loss to Tulsa. Portnoy: OregonOregon got a scare from Boise State last week, but there's no way that's happening two weeks in a row. Oklahoma State looked atrocious last week in Eric Morris' debut at Tulsa. I'd be shocked if the Ducks don't roll in this one. No. 15 BYU vs. Arizona When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo, UtahLine: BYU -7.5 Young: BYUI trust the BYU defense more than I trust quarterback Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense. Litman: BYUQuarterback Bear Bachmeier and the Cougars have to win their first Big 12 game to keep pace with the likes of Texas Tech and Houston, and will take care of business against Arizona. Cohen: BYUThis is an important early-season mile marker for BYU in its quest to supplant Texas Tech in the Big 12 hierarchy. A controlled win over Arizona should give the Cougars plenty of confidence at the start of conference play. Portnoy: BYUIf BYU is really going to challenge for the Big 12 title, this is the kind of game the Cougars need to win. Arizona was much improved last year and Noah Fifita is back, but I think BYU's talent advantage outweighs that. Illinois vs. Duke When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FS1)Where: Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign, IllinoisLine: Illinois -5.5 Young: DukeThe defending ACC champs — Duke! — have a bona fide star at running back in Nate Sheppard and the Illinois defense gave up 24 first downs and 194 rushing yards to UAB in its opener. Litman: IllinoisQuarterback Katin Houser builds on his four-TD performance against UAB in Week 1 against the Darian Mensah-less Duke Blue Devils. Cohen: IllinoisHow popular is Illinois football right now? Illinois sold out Memorial Stadium for this week's non-conference tilt against Duke. A crowd like that should push head coach Bret Bielema's squad to a win. Portnoy: IllinoisKatin Houser put up huge numbers at East Carolina and his Big Ten return is off to a nice start. I like what Bret Bielema and this staff did with Luke Altmyer and Houser feels like a nice replacement. Duke has some talent, but Illinois is the better team here. Syracuse vs. Cal When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (USA Net)Where: JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse, New YorkLine: Syracuse -3.5 Young: SyracuseHead coach Fran Brown has his quarterback in Steve Angeli, and his quarterback is healthy. Angeli can be as good as Kyle McCord was at ‘Cuse if he stays healthy, and I like this matchup for a veteran head coach against a rookie one, in Cal’s Tosh Lupoi, coming off a loss and traveling across three time zones. Litman: SyracuseAn early season classic ACC matchup! Orange quarterback Steve Angeli keeps up momentum from a strong Week 1 performance as Cal falls to 0-2 in the Tosh Lupoi era. Cohen: CalFool me once (as the Bears did last week), shame on you. Fool me twice (as I back the Bears again this week), shame on me. They should bounce back with a win. Portnoy: CalTosh Lupoi's team didn't exactly help my case for the Golden Bears as potential ACC contenders with their loss to UCLA last week, but I'm riding with the "Calgorithm" again. Fran Brown's team should be much improved with Steve Angeli, but I think Lupoi's bunch bounce back after a tough opener. Boise State vs. Memphis When: Saturday, 6 p.m. ET (USA Network)Where: Albertsons Stadium, Boise, IdahoLine: Boise State -8.5 Young: Boise StateI saw enough from the Broncos to believe they're one of the two best teams in the Group of Six. Sadly, Memphis is not one of those two teams. Litman: Boise StateComing off an impressive performance from Week 1 where they almost knocked off then-No. 2 Oregon in Eugene, the Broncos get into the win column. Cohen: Boise StateThe Broncos played incredibly on the road at Oregon last week to establish themselves as legitimate CFP contenders from the Group of Six. Memphis wants to be viewed in that same category after knocking off UNLV in its season opener. Boise State is a cut above. Portnoy: Boise StateI'm rolling with the Broncos until proven otherwise. This team is as experienced as any in the Group of Six, and they looked the part last week at Oregon. Could there be a letdown? Sure, but I think Boise State will be able to run the ball more effectively against Memphis, and that gives the Broncos the edge. No. 4 Texas vs. No. 1 Ohio State When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TexasLine: Texas -1.5 Young: Ohio StateThe Buckeyes' weakness is on the offensive line. However, the cheat code exists. Quarterback Julian Sayin doesn't have to punch up the "Konami code." Just press four. Jeremiah Smith will beat the game. Litman: TexasArch Manning and the Texas defense aren't about to let Ohio State beat them a third straight time in less than two years. Cohen: Ohio StateA year ago, new defensive coordinator Matt Patricia put the clamps on Texas' offense. This time, new Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will unleash a few wrinkles the Longhorns aren't ready for. The Buckeyes get it done. Portnoy: TexasIf not now, when? That's how I feel about Texas and its national title aspirations. Saturday's game is a chance to cement the Longhorns as the top team in the country. articles.title: Durham on course for promotion against Middlesex
articles.summary: Durham are on course to secure promotion from Division Two after setting Middlesex a huge target of 424 at the Riverside.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, Banks Homes Riverside (day three)

Durham 252 & 374 McKinney 184, Ackermann 48; Higgins 4-79

Middlesex 203: Holden 43, Duke 38*; Carse 5-72, Raine 3-67 & 55-2

Middlesex (3pts) need another 369 to beat Durham (4 pts) with eight wickets standing

Durham need eight wickets to secure promotion back to County Championship Division One after Ben McKinney's magnificent 184 reasserted the hosts' dominance over Middlesex on the third day at the Riverside.

McKinney picked up from where he left off on day two and while Middlesex took a couple of wickets, they could not dislodge the Durham opener until the last ball before lunch as he made his second highest first-class score.

Middlesex struck back with the second new ball after lunch before a brief rain delay halted proceedings.

A gritty 48 from Colin Ackermann then helped Durham set the visitors an imposing target of 424 after they were bowled out for 374, with Ryan Higgins the pick of the bowlers for the visitors.

Brydon Carse then saw off both Middlesex openers to move Durham closer to promotion, but bad light denied the hosts the chance to pick up any more wickets.

Durham resumed on 204-2, with unbeaten centurion McKinney and Mayank Agarwal the batters at the crease. In the early stages of play, they looked to build on their lead of 253 and McKinney added to his boundary tally as he nudged the lead towards 300.

However, Middlesex took two much-needed wickets as Tom Helm got Agarwal caught behind and Higgins removed Graham Clark's off-stump.

McKinney passed 150 for the second time this season, with Ackermann joining the centurion in the middle as Durham continued to build their lead, but eventually when he tried to accelerate the scoring off the bowling of Luke Hollman and was caught when he mistimed a shot and Max Holden took the catch.

Naavya Sharma removed Ollie Robinson lbw when Middlesex took the second new ball after the lunch and Kasey Aldridge followed, caught at second slip off Tom Helm.

Following a rain interruption, Ackermann and Carse stretched Durham's lead past 400.

But Higgins then struck twice, dismissing both Carse and Ben Raine, before Ackermann then fell two runs short of a half-century as he was caught behind off Seb Morgan.

Middlesex's second innings nearly got off to a nightmare start as Hollman drove a Raine delivery towards Clark at backward point, but he could not cling on to a regulation catch.

Carse had Hollman caught behind soon after, though, and struck again when Sam Robson edged to Robinson behind the stumps.

The players then went off for bad light and play was abandoned with Durham requiring eight wickets to secure promotion, while Middlesex need 369 runs to win.

articles.title: Browns' QB Deshaun Watson's future career in the balance in 2026
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson speaks on the pressure he is facing heading into next season.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is staring down a career-defining season in 2026. Watson is entering the season on the final year of his contract in Cleveland, and the Browns have their first "out" in his seemingly never-ending contract at the end of this season.

Watson has done next to nothing in the past four years that would warrant another contract with Cleveland or another contract, period, with anyone in the NFL. His career is very much on the line, and he knows it.

On Wednesday, Watson spoke about his expectations heading into the season and how he is viewing the year. He said, "Me being on the last year of my deal and being year 10, I feel like this is my opportunity to be able to go and showcase that I can still play in this league, and I want to continue to play in this league. So this is my opportunity to do that."

That is one element of the entire Deshaun Watson discussion that gets lost in the shuffle. He is not a young player in this league anymore. He is turning 31 in just a couple of days and is simply a shadow of his former self.

What made Watson so good in his time in Houston was his ability to create plays with his athleticism. That goes away with age, but it also goes away with Watson's lengthy injury history.

All of this is to say that Watson has to adapt, and this is his last chance to do so. His leash with Todd Monken is going to be short, and he will have very limited time to prove that there is still a good quarterback somewhere inside him. It is very unlikely that even if things go decently this year, he will be back in Cleveland. That is, of course, unless he leads the Browns to a playoff berth.

For Cleveland, they are just yearning for good quarterback play from someone. Whether it is Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders , or Taylen Green , they just need decent quarterback play.

For Watson specifically, he desperately needs good quarterback play. If he plays well, he will have an opportunity at a very small contract somewhere next year. If he struggles, it might be time for the former promising star quarterback to consider life after football.

articles.title: Hamilton and Leclerc 'squash' Monza controversy
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" any controversy between them from the Italian Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" any controversy between them after a difficult Italian Grand Prix.

Leclerc forced Hamilton into the gravel at the first chicane at Monza on Sunday, and then crashed two laps later. Hamilton recovered to finish a disappointed sixth.

It was the second flashpoint between the Ferrari drivers in two races, after an argument over the radio during the Dutch Grand Prix when Leclerc resisted a request to move aside for Hamilton.

Hamilton said: "What's great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion. We sat face to face, just him and I, and talked about it.

"We were just both open and honest, and we squashed it. We can move on. I think that one shows the maturity from him."

Speaking at the media day for this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix, the seven-time champion added: "It's healthy. It's a relationship we have built over time. Of course, there's going to be frustrations and I'm sure there'll be more times where we're close because we're very close in pace.

"We both want to win just as much as each other, and we both want to do well for the team as well."

Leclerc said: "It's kind of clear that we never want to see a car of the same team in the grass.

"After reviewing, we spoke with Lewis. I obviously know I went too far in turn two and I said it to Lewis and I think it's very clear what we should do or should avoid going forward.

"But I won't go into much more details of what we've said. The only thing I can say is that it definitely did not affect the good relationship that we have and it will not affect anything going forward. And that is the most important for me, really.

"I know we are driving for Ferrari and if there's one race where you don't want that to happen, it's in Monza and when these things happen at our home race, then it does a huge mess outside.

"However, looking at the race from outside, there's been also some friction between other team-mates and the only thing we end up speaking of is Lewis and me, which I don't think is quite right. But that doesn't mean we did everything perfect."

Hamilton acknowledged again that Ferrari had to improve their operations, after three consecutive race weekends where qualifying has not gone to plan.

"It's really just making sure we're executing to make sure we get the best result for the team," he said. "Instead of us working against each other and finish fourth and fifth, maybe we can work together and get a podium and pull off more points.

"It's a longer term process. It's not something we can just change into this weekend. There's a huge amount of moving parts, there's a lot of people, there's a culture that's been there for a long, long time and moving big pieces is not so easy."

Madring 'one of the most risky circuits'

F1 faces a fresh challenge this weekend at the first Spanish Grand at the new Madring, a hybrid street circuit built on the Ifema complex near the city's international airport.

Hamilton said: "It's a massively challenging circuit. Of all the new tracks that I've gone to, this one, maybe Saudi, are the two closest in terms of how difficult it was to get on top of the car and find the right lines and such."

Mercedes driver George Russell said: "It's a crazy circuit, I would put it. Arguably one of the most risky circuits of the whole calendar.

"Because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque, the walls are very close, so there's no margin for error, but then you have other corners... where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone, you're braking and turning at the same time, so locking tyres are going to be easy and if you lock up you'll be straight in the wall.

"So, excited to try that out, I think it's going to be really challenging for us as drivers, the race is going to be challenging to overtake, so on the whole it's not an easy one."

Russell heads into the race 66 points behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli after the Italian's landmark victory in Monza from 19th on the grid.

The Briton acknowledged that his title hopes with nine or 10 races left, amid uncertainty about the end of the season, were fading fast.

"I would definitely need some luck and I need some good performances," Russell said. "It's not really something I'm thinking about, because he's performing better than me, so he deserves to be leading the championship.

"There's still a long way to go, but he's yet to have a bad weekend in terms of performance.

"So he's performing exceptionally well, my performances are better, but if I want to win this championship, I'm going to need some luck on the way. But it's not something I'm focused on. I'm focused on driving faster and just finding more performance."

Antonelli said: "I don't really want to try thinking about the championship. I think Monza was the proof that I wasn't driving thinking about, or worrying about the championship. I was just driving to win, to do my best. So that's the mindset."

The Italian said his win in Monza was "so far the best day of my life and definitely one I will remember forever".

He said a day karting with Mercedes on Monday helped him move on from the excitement of the day before.

"After Monza, that night, that day overall, I was very excited. But then going karting on Monday helped me to go back to earth, just go back to the ground.

"It was a good day, good fun day with the team. It was also a way to remind myself where I came from, all the journey that was done.

"And then about pressure, I try to embrace it as much as possible. And I try to see it as a positive thing and try to see it as an opportunity too. That's also what is helping me to stay calm under difficult situations."

articles.title: Romeo Doubs admits he 'wasn't locked in enough' on pivotal drop in Patriots debut
articles.summary: Making his Patriots debut after signing a $68 million contract,. Romeo Doubs addressed his costly fourth-quarter drop against Seattle.
articles.body:
The start to Romeo Doubs ' tenure with the New England Patriots went from underwhelming to disappointing in the span of just a single target. While Drake Maye's primary targets in the 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks were A.J. Brown before his injury, DeMario Douglas , Rhamondre Stevenson and Mack Hollins , Doubs was a non-factor for much of the game.

Given that Doubs signed a four-year, $68 million contract with the Patriots this offseason, this was a bit baffling. However, while Doubs finished the night with three targets, he had a brutal drop in the fourth quarter with the game tied at 10-10. That drop was followed up by the second of three fourth-quarter interceptions Maye threw.

Unsurprisingly, virtually every NFL fan watching the game was quick to point out not only his free-agency contract but also his lack of production, as he finished with no catches. After the game, Doubs was asked about the pivotal drop and vowed to be better.

"No. Like I said, I just wasn't locked in enough on the football," Doubs said. "The results speak for themselves. I'll be better moving forward."

For good measure, while Doubs' drop was a rough play and a big opportunity to keep moving the ball, it was the fourth quarter as a whole that doomed the Patriots. Maye's three interceptions were brutal, and his final one came with the team trailing 13-10 and already in field goal position.

There is no shortage of issues the Patriots need to fix following Week 1, and there's also an unknown surrounding wide receiver A.J. Brown's injury , which sidelined him for the bulk of the second half.

articles.title: Why Athletics will let $2.85 million former Yankees reliever walk in free agency
articles.summary: This seems like an obvious decision for the A's.
articles.body:
The Athletics need to improve their pitching staff to contend in 2027.

That could mean spending a little bit more in free agency or making trades for controllable relievers.

However, the A's have just one more season in West Sacramento before making the big move to Las Vegas.

Will ownership be willing to have a higher payroll next year, or will they wait for when the AL West club moves to Vegas?

Whichever route they decide, the A's could use a few proven high-leverage relievers this offseason.

They could consider bringing back right-hander Mark Leiter Jr. , but FanSided's Zachary Rotman predicts they will let the former New York Yankee walk in free agency.

"The Athletics could look at how Leiter pitched down the stretch of his season and attempt to bring him back, but this right-hander is set to hit free agency in the offseason and is a 35-year-old without an exciting track record," Rotman wrote.

"If the price is right, there're worse relievers they can sign, but the A's should be looking to upgrade. That means letting Leiter go and replacing him with someone better, even if John Fisher has to spend a little bit more money."

Leiter suffered a season-ending hip injury and underwent surgery in July. He posted a 4.28 ERA in 36 appearances out of the A's bullpen but allowed just one run in his final 18 innings.

Leiter would be a cheap option for the A's, but the bullpen could use someone with more firepower for the later innings of ballgames.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel: A.J. Brown still undergoing tests, unsure of Week 2 availability
articles.summary: While a report indicated Patriots receiver A.J.
articles.body:
While a report indicated Patriots receiver A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain, head coach Mike Vrabel declined to confirm that in his Thursday press conference.

Vrabel noted that Brown 's upcoming availability is in question after he suffered an ankle injury during Wednesday night's loss to the Seahawks. But beyond that, the club is still evaluating the receiver.

"We're running more tests, but we'll update you here next week," Vrabel said. "Wasn't able to finish the game, and we'll continue to evaluate, continue to run tests. But I don't know if he'll be available going forward here for the next week, but we'll see.

"I know he'll do everything that he can to get back as quickly as possible. And once we get the report, then we'll figure out what the treatment plan is."

Brown suffered his ankle injury early in the third quarter on Wednesday night. He was able to walk off the field and into the locker room for further evaluation.

The veteran wideout finished with three catches for 26 yards in his Patriots debut.

New England will face Pittsburgh at home in Week 2.

articles.title: USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino claims he is 'always open to help' Tottenham regardless of division
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has confirmed he was approached to take the Tottenham Hotspur job last season — but the U.S. Men's National Team boss says he was fully c...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has revealed he would have accepted the Tottenham Hotspur job — even if the club had been playing in the EFL Championship.

U.S. Men's National Team head coach Pochettino confirmed he did receive an approach to return to Spurs last season when the club was embroiled in a relegation battle. However, Pochettino stressed he was fully committed to steering the U.S. into the FIFA World Cup and has since signed a contract through 2030 due to his deep satisfaction with the position.

When asked whether he would have accepted the Spurs job in the Championship, he stated, via The Mirror : "Yes, of course. Tottenham? Yes, of course. It's the only club that always I am open to help. Whatever division. Another club, no. But Tottenham, yes."

Former Spurs manager Pochettino, who spent five years at Tottenham and remains beloved by the club's supporters, has previously indicated his desire to one day return to the North London club.

However, Pochettino maintains the timing has never aligned — and that was the situation when he received the call following Thomas Frank's dismissal. "Yeah, but in this moment they called everyone, they called all the coaches! Free and not free!"

Tottenham endured a brief and disastrous stint under Igor Tudor before Roberto De Zerbi was appointed to revitalize the club's fortunes. Yet Pochettino, having initially expressed a desire to return to club management, has grown increasingly committed to his role as USMNT boss, developing an even deeper passion for the position throughout the World Cup.

Pochettino, alongside his backroom staff including trusted assistant Jesus Perez, helped joint hosts the U.S. top their group and advance to the Round of 16 before falling to Belgium . The former Spurs manager revealed he chose to remain with the USMNT due to the backing from the federation as well as the overwhelming support from supporters throughout the tournament.

Pochettino said: "One thing that changed our mind: the people. The human beings in the federation. Because before the start of the World Cup we met the whole board, the federation board in New York, before starting working with the players in Atlanta.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"And they offered us to do four more years. I said, 'Yeah but if we lose all the games in the World Cup...' But they said, 'No, we trust in you, we trust in your job, we trust in your vision, in the way that you behave. You stayed here when it was possible to move somewhere else.'

"When we finished the World Cup, our vision was completely different because we created something. The fans were amazing. The people were so excited. The players changed their mindset. After one week, the federation called and we said, 'We are ready for it.'"

His enthusiasm for the role is unmistakable. He retains a fondness for Tottenham and even extends sympathy toward former chairman Daniel Levy following his removal from the club. "I think he feels like [I did] when I was sacked! Now he knows the feeling," said Pochettino. "I am sorry for him."

Pochettino even conceded that he might one day entertain the idea of taking charge of the England national team . Remarkably, this comes despite being Argentinian — and the lingering tensions stemming from the World Cup semi-final.

He stated: "One thing I don't want, because the USA guys will kill me, if the headline is: 'Mauricio will consider English job.' No, it is like I am considering it now. One day if I am free.

"For me it is because we are very similar in the way we feel the passion of football. I think we are very similar. I love the countryside, I love the farms, and here it is amazing. I think you respect all the things that I also grow up with in my country.

"It is true it can be controversial because an Argentinian guy is thinking to maybe one day defend the flag of England and we were involved in a war..."

articles.title: Behind the Numbers: Cowboys at Giants Week 1
articles.summary: It is so awesome that Week 1 is finally here.
articles.body:
Each week, we'll examine the numbers surrounding the Cowboys and their next opponent on the schedule. This data includes historical points as well as more recent numbers that may indicate which team has the edge in the upcoming matchup.

The Cowboys lead the head-to-head matchup with the Giants all-time 78-48-2.

The Dak Prescott -led Cowboys are 14-3 against the Giants. Two of those losses came in Dak's rookie campaign while the other came in 2025. In that matchup, the Cowboys had already been eliminated from the postseason and Dak was pulled at halftime.

In 17 games, Dak Prescott has thrown for 4,346 yards, 31 touchdowns, 9 interceptions, and has a passer rating of 101.5 . These are some of the best numbers that the Cowboys quarterback has against any team in the NFL.

The new Giants head coach John Harbaugh is 4-1 against the Cowboys. The single loss came in 2016 during Dak Prescott's rookie season.

Week 2 of 2025 featured a ferocious display of offensive fireworks with an NFL record tying six lead changes. Dallas would go on to win this game in overtime off the leg of Brandon Aubrey .

New York has won zero of their Week 1 home openers since their last victory in 2010. This losing streak includes a 40-0 loss against the Cowboys in 2023.

The Giants have won just three home games against the Cowboys since 2016. Dak Prescott played a total of six quarters in those three losses.

Last season, the Giants had a record of 3-5 at MetLife Stadium. They were 3-3 at home with Jaxson Dart at the helm.

Dak Prescott finished the 2025 season with 32 total touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

Led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , Dallas finished with the number two ranked passing offense in the NFL.

Javonte Williams led the rushing attack with 1,201 yards on the ground. This was good enough to finish ninth in yards among all running backs.

Continuity is key for the Cowboys offense in 2026. This front office lost zero offensive starters from last year's roster. The one meaningful change is that Tyler Smith will now be out for 4-6 weeks with the thumb injury.

In 12 starts, Jaxson Dart finished his rookie campaign with 24 total touchdowns. Nine of those touchdowns were scored on the ground. He threw only five interceptions.

Dart was sacked nearly three times per game last season.

The Giants run game averaged an impressive 129.1 yards per game ( fifth in the NFL).

New York ranked 17 th in scoring offense and 26 th in scoring defense.

The Cowboys are the clear favorites on paper. Even without Tyler Smith, the Cowboys possess too much firepower for the Giants to match. Dak has been dominant against the Giants throughout his 10-year career. Some of his best performances have come against this NFC East rival. There is little reason to expect a different result considering the weapons Dallas possesses.

Defensively, this will be Christian Parker's first game calling plays. The question this season will be how quickly this defense can reach its full potential. The Giants offense may have some ability to create big-time plays throughout the game depending on the health of Malik Nabers , but Dallas will most likely see a heavy run-first committee approach from John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy.

That backfield features both power and speed with the mix of Cam Skattebo , Najee Harris , and Tyrone Tracy Jr. Jaxson Dart can also catch fire if you allow him to utilize his legs. The good news for the Cowboys is the new defense was built to stop the run first and foremost. If they're able to do that with consistent light boxes, Dallas should expect to keep the Giants run-heavy offense quite limited.

This is week one of the new NFL season, so last year's stats will only contribute so much to the story that is about to unfold in front of our eyes. However, the tale of Dak Prescott and the Cowboys over the last decade paints a clear and consistent picture versus the Giants. That picture tells us that Dallas should win this game convincingly.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson shares support for Falcons quarterbacks
articles.summary: Bijan Robinson on Falcons QBs: 'My job is to make sure they are supported'
articles.body:
When Tua Tagovailoa takes the field on Sunday it will mark the sixth straight season that the Atlanta Falcons have a different starting quarterback. After Matt Ryan 's final season in Atlanta in 2021, the Falcons went with Marcus Mariota , followed by Desmond Ridder , then Kirk Cousins , before Michael Penix Jr. last year.

The one constant in the backfield for the last three seasons has been the best player on the Falcons' roster, superstar running back Bijan Robinson .

Asked about the team's constantly-changing QB situation, Robinson responded that it's his job to make sure that they feel supported, no matter who's sharing the backfield with him, per Josh Kendall at The Athletic .

"I just make sure I am here to support them no matter what," said Robinson. "My job is to make sure they are supported when I talk to the media so they can feel confident going into it."

Robinson said he also believes that Atlanta's strong supporting cast will help Tagovailoa get comfortable.

"He has a lot of talent around him, and I think it's going to make him a lot more confident," added Robinson. "It's just him having that trust in us to put the ball in our hands."

Unless Tagovailoa stuns the NFL world's low expectations of him and establishes himself as the Falcons' franchise QB, we will almost certainly see Michael Penix Jr. on the field again at some point this season.

Should Penix flop as well, then there's a chance we'll see yet another starter emerge later this year in the form of undrafted rookie Jack Strand, who was the team's most impressive QB during the preseason. Some analysts believe that Strand could wind up starting more games than either Penix or Tagovailoa.

If Strand emerges as a legitimate starter it would come as a surprise, but if the Falcons get a true QB1 out of it nobody should complain.

Until then, this will remain Bijan Robinson's team.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers declares MAGA movement dead as he rants about Trump, Obama, COVID, Colin Kaepernick
articles.summary: There is no doubt that Aaron Rodgers is full of opinions, and he recently declared Donald Trump’s MAGA movement dead while also taking aim at the likes of f...
articles.body:
There is no doubt that Aaron Rodgers is full of opinions , and he recently declared Donald Trump 's MAGA movement dead while also taking aim at the likes of former President Barack Obama , COVID-19, and Colin Kaepernick .

During an appearance on Not Just Football, which is hosted by his Pittsburgh Steelers teammate Cam Heyward , Rodgers went on a lengthy rant .

"There is no MAGA movement; there is no 'Make America Great Again' movement because the guy you elected hasn't done any of his campaign promises," he said, before later criticizing Obama and his failed promises. "When Obama was president, everybody's like, 'Oh, there's gonna be hope and change for a better world.' Has anything in the Black community gotten significantly better? Is anybody better off? Did the Affordable Care Act make a major difference in the world besides being an extra tax for the rich?"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Rodgers doesn't appear to like either president before seemingly alluding to Dr. Anthony Fauci and the COVID-19 pandemic, calling the former an "old bag of bones." He appears to believe that the pandemic was a "multi-trillion-dollar worldwide" experiment conducted "to see how much they can control us."

He also theorized that politics are just a "crazy setup." Rodgers used a quote he remembered: "If voting actually mattered, they wouldn't let you do it."

The Steelers' quarterback thinks we should all be "skeptical" of what politicians tell us. He knows he'll get flak for his opinions, saying that non-NFC North fans who don't like him are upset at him because of his opinions on the COVID-19 vaccine .

Ultimately, Rodgers is going to continue speaking his truth. Earlier in the episode, the Steelers quarterback was asked about what it's like to be a polarizing figure in the NFL. He even mentioned his take on Kaepernick, whom he supported after he protested the National Anthem, saying he was "one of the best 64 quarterbacks" in the league at the time.

articles.title: Red Sox's Sonny Gray Comments On Potential Retirement After Season
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox traded for Sonny Gray in the offseason, and he has been a great addition
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox traded for Sonny Gray in the offseason, and he has been a great addition.

Gray has a 2.69 ERA in his 14th season and has made 26 starts so far for the Red Sox. He has been a very reliable starter in his first season with the Red Sox, but the 36-year-old does not know what his future holds. He has a $30 million option next season, but has noted that he will retire if his family wants him to.

"I'll be done in a heartbeat," Gray told The Boston Globe's Alex Speier when asked what he would do if his family wants him at home year-round.

Gray has played in 371 games, including the postseason, and has been named an All-Star three times. He has not undergone Tommy John surgery, which is almost unheard of nowadays, especially for someone like Gray who has pitched so many innings. However, he has never won a World Series. The Red Sox should be playing baseball in October, and Gray is focused on helping the team do something worth remembering. He is unsure if he will be back next season, so he is making the most of the moment.

"We'll see what the future holds for me," he said. "But if this is it, no better way to go out and try to do something special here the next couple months."

The Red Sox season, at one point, seemed like a lost cause and Gray was a trade candidate. However, the team has turned things around and has a real chance to make a run in October.

articles.title: Padres news: San Diego pitcher gets big injury update as playoff push continues
