The San Diego Padres could be getting an important piece of their bullpen back at exactly the right time. Right-handed reliever Jason Adam continues to make progress from the right shoulder strain that has kept him on the injured list since the beginning of July.

According to MLB.com, Adam threw his third bullpen session off the Petco Park mound on Sept. 7 and is scheduled to face hitters in Arizona on Sept. 10. That's a big step toward a potential return.

Adam has been one of San Diego 's most important late-inning relievers since joining the organization. When healthy, he's capable of handling high-leverage situations and serving as the bridge to the back end of the bullpen.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Padres have managed without him, but getting Adam back would make an already dangerous relief corps even deeper.

San Diego currently has Mason Miller and Adrian Morejon handling many of its biggest late-game situations. Adding Adam back into that mix would give manager Craig Stammen another trusted option when protecting a lead. Bradgley Rodriguez has filled Adam's role tremendously. But those innings are only becoming more important.

The Padres improved to 78-68 after completing a three-game sweep of the Washington Nationals on Wednesday, extending their winning streak to four games as they continue fighting for an NL Wild Card spot.

There are still hurdles for Adam to clear before he returns to the active roster, but facing hitters represents another meaningful step in the right direction. San Diego doesn't need Adam to rush back.

The Padres need him healthy for the games that matter most.

Miguel Andujar, the Padres' DH , should return from his injury very soon as well.

articles.title: Patriots news: Drake Maye's rough opener has Will Campbell silver lining
articles.summary: On Wednesday evening, the New England Patriots choked a double-digit second-half lead and dropped their first game of the season to the Seattle Seahawks in a...
articles.body:
On Wednesday evening, the New England Patriots choked a double-digit second-half lead and dropped their first game of the season to the Seattle Seahawks in a rematch of last year's Super Bowl. Quarterback Drake Maye tossed three interceptions in the fourth quarter alone, including a brutal decision on a late third down when New England was in position to at least tie the game with a field goal.

However, it wasn't all bad news on the offensive side of the ball for New England.

" Will Campbell allowed just 1 pressure on 44 pass block snaps last night, a major improvement over the 8 pressures he allowed in the Super Bowl. He's on pace for a leap forward in year 2 now that he's fully healthy," reported NFL Draft Files on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Indeed, Campbell looked much better on Wednesday night than he did in the Super Bowl against the same Seahawks' defensive front, after which he drew immense criticism for his poor performance.

As NFL Draft Files referenced, Campbell was dealing with an injury in that contest, so that could explain at least part of the improvement, although he has also clearly spent time working on his game this offseason.

"Biggest improvement is timing up the snap count and getting a good jump… it's so important to put yourself in a good position to not have to rush. And it's incredibly hard to do in Seattle. Very encouraging night for Will," noted TJ Lang on X.

While this is certainly a positive development, it also makes it all the more troubling that Maye had such a rough close to the game despite having much more time in the pocket.

In any case, the Patriots will next hit the field on September 20 against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

articles.title: England close in on Pakistan whitewash in third Test as Robinson shines
articles.summary: Demoralised tourists reach 52-2 before rain ends play early on day two, needing 268 runs to make England bat again.
articles.body:
Ollie Robinson continued his outstanding summer with two wickets in his opening over as England pushed Pakistan towards ⁠defeat in the third Test ⁠at Edgbaston.

Robinson, man of the match in the first two Tests , struck with the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings on Thursday and again three deliveries later to leave England closing in on a 3-0 series ⁠whitewash.

The demoralised tourists reached 52-2 before rain ended play early on day two, needing 268 runs to make England bat again.

Robinson, 32, has been almost unplayable in this series, taking 21 wickets at an average of under seven runs each.

He continued in the same ⁠vein in Birmingham, removing Saim Ayub, who was dismissed for a duck in both innings, and then Abdullah Shafique to finish the day with figures of 2-10 from his six overs.

“He’s probably one of the most consistent bowlers in world cricket. He knows what he’s doing with the ball, and he wears you down a bit so it’s a challenge,” said Pakistan batting coach Mike Smith.

“He has bowled exceptionally well, and he’s in a little purple patch as a player. We need to find a way to combat that as well as we can.”

Shan Masood, who was dropped at slip by Ben Duckett off Gus Atkinson, was still there on 21 at the close, alongside opener Azan Awais on 29, but Pakistan’s position appears hopeless.

England, who led by 23 overnight, had earlier pressed the accelerator to extend their first-innings advantage to a daunting 320.

They made 453 with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence extending their fifth-wicket partnership to 86 until Brook set off for an impossible single and was run out by Masood for 75 from ⁠97 balls.

Lawrence went on to make 65 from 82 balls before dragging a wide ball onto his ⁠stumps to give Mohammad Imran his first Test wicket. It was a third Test half-century in a row for Lawrence, who was recalled after a two-year absence for this series.

“I’m really happy with how I’ve contributed,” said Lawrence. “I was feeling really good today, got on a bit of a roll with Brooky and ⁠went with it.

“I thought I was going to make a really big score, to be honest. It wasn’t to be, but I think if I’d been offered 65 at the start of the ⁠day, I’d have taken it.”

There was also a welcome half-century from the out-of-form Jamie ⁠Smith, who overcame an uncertain start and a finger injury, which caused him to hand over the wicketkeeping gloves to Jordan Cox, to strike 69 off 84 balls including one six and nine fours.

It was his highest Test score since a second-innings 88 against India on the same ground 14 months ago.

Robinson chimed in with ‌a 50 of his own, which included a huge six into the Hollies Stand off Mohammad Abbas, before becoming Razaullah’s fourth victim.

The blooding of the 21-year-old, who had only played eight first-class games prior to his call-up, was one of the few positives for ‌Pakistan.

While ‌he was expensive – he conceded 148 runs off his 23 overs – he posed a threat with his pace and aggression.

Razaullah may represent a brighter future for Pakistan, but the present remains bleak for a team that has lost 15 of its last 20 Tests.

articles.title: Weight-loss drugs in sport: Ozempic, Mounjaro not on Wada banned list for athletes
articles.summary: Athletes will not be banned from using weight-loss drugs, but the substances will remain on a monitoring list.
articles.body:
Athletes will not be banned from taking weight-loss drugs under the World Anti-Doping Agency's rules for 2027, but the substances will remain on its monitoring list.

Wada confirmed the decision following a meeting of its executive committee as it continues to examine the potential of the drugs, known as GLP-1 receptor agonists, to enhance performance and the risk of abuse in sport.

The rules take effect in January and are reviewed annually.

Medications such as Ozempic and Mounjaro have become increasingly common outside elite sport.

The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams revealed last year - while on a break from professional tennis - that she had been using weight-loss medication.

Professor Olivier Rabin, Wada's senior director for science and medicine, warned athletes to be "very careful using those drugs and never without medical advice and supervision".

"It's such a drastic change in your physiology that it can come with serious side effects and risks, in particular for athletes," he told BBC Sport.

Semaglutide, often marketed under the Ozempic and Wegovy banners, was first placed on Wada's monitoring list in 2024. Tirzepatide, commonly branded as Mounjaro, was added this year.

For a substance to move from the monitoring list to the prohibited list, it needs to meet two of three criteria: that it can enhance sport performance, it poses a health risk to an athlete, or it violates the spirit of sport.

Wada has started one study and is preparing another to examine the effects of the drugs in conditions designed to mimic high-level exercise.

"It's still going to take us a little bit of time to collect all this information, because they are highly controlled studies in very specific conditions," said Rabin.

"What we want to see is whether some of the pharmacological impact on human physiology that has been observed in obese patients would also occur in non-obese, highly trained people."

Rabin said potential benefits could also be offset by side effects such as nausea, fatigue and the loss of muscle mass.

"If you're an athlete and you lose muscle mass, that may be very counterproductive for what you're trying to achieve," he said.

"So all these elements show you that it's not a very straightforward answer."

Under the usual timetable, a change approved at next September's executive committee meeting would take effect in January 2028.

Which sports could be at risk of misuse?

Weight-loss drugs seem most likely to appeal to athletes in weight-category sports such as boxing and wrestling, as well as horse racing, where jockeys have to meet strict weight requirements.

"A lot of sports would benefit from weight control and weight management," said Rabin.

"Not only those in weight-category sports, but all sorts of sports."

He highlighted long-distance runners and cyclists as other athletes with weight control "very high on their agenda".

"There are sports as well where aesthetics play a role," he said. "It can be gymnastics, can be horse riding, can be many different sports where you don't have weight categories, but physical appearance is quite important."

Very few athletes have spoken publicly about using weight-loss drugs. The most high-profile is Williams, who said she struggled to lose weight after having children.

She is also a spokesperson for Ro, a company which sells GLP-1s and in which her husband is an investor.

A recent Loughborough University study, , external which surveyed more than 100 sports medicine physicians around the world, found 12% were aware of athletes using GLP-1 drugs despite having no medical need for them.

articles.title: Joel Klatt: Kyle Whittingham 'Not Tied To' Bryce Underwood Amid QB Struggles
articles.summary: Joel Klatt joined "The Herd" to discuss the relationship between Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham and QB Bryce Underwood.
articles.body: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham did not recruit Bryce Underwood. He wasn't involved in the massive NIL deal that brought Underwood to Ann Arbor. And he certainly wasn't the coach who named the former No. 1 overall recruit the starting quarterback as a true freshman. That could make what happens next between Whittingham and Underwood — who struggled in the Wolverines' narrow Week 1 win over in-state foe Western Michigan — particularly interesting. "Kyle Whittingham is not tied to Bryce Underwood," FOX Sports lead college football analyst Joel Klatt said Wednesday on "The Herd." "It was not Kyle's decision to give Bryce Underwood the NIL deal. He's not as tied to Underwood as the previous coaching staff." That dynamic could come into focus quickly Saturday, when Michigan hosts No. 11 Oklahoma in one of the most intriguing games of Week 2. Underwood's first game under Whittingham didn't exactly go according to plan. The sophomore quarterback — recruited to Michigan by former head coach Sherrone Moore and his staff — completed just 12 of 22 passes for 170 yards, one touchdown and two turnovers in the win. Earlier this week, Whittingham made it clear that Underwood's status as Michigan's starting quarterback isn't necessarily permanent. "He's our QB right now, and it's not something that's infinite," Whittingham said. "At some point, we've got to turn a corner." Underwood appeared surprised Wednesday when a reporter asked him about his coach's comments. "There were comments about that?" Underwood said. "That's cool. I didn't see that. It's cool." So, how will this all play out when Underwood and the Wolverines go up against one of the top defenses in the country Saturday afternoon in Ann Arbor? "I think that makes this week interesting," Klatt said. "How effective is he? How long does he stay in the game if he is ineffective? That's a question." This is new territory for Whittingham, who arrived at Michigan after 20 seasons at Utah, where he became the winningest coach in program history. He inherited Underwood and the rest of the Wolverines' roster when he took over in Ann Arbor. Klatt believes that distinction matters, as Whittingham isn't simply tasked with deciding whether Underwood is talented enough to be Michigan's starting quarterback. He's tasked with figuring out how to put him in the best possible position to succeed. "I'm a firm believer that the best coaches put their players in the best position to be successful," Klatt said. "So you've got to decide: What can our guy do well … and now let's build a system around what he can do well." That is where Michigan appeared to struggle in Week 1. "What it looked like against Western Michigan was oil and water," Klatt said. "You have a quarterback running a system that just didn't look like it was gelling." That will need to change on Saturday as Michigan won't have the luxury of easing its way into its Week 2 matchup against standout quarterback John Mateer and the No. 11-ranked Sooners. If Underwood struggles again, the question Klatt raised becomes increasingly relevant: How much patience does Whittingham have?

articles.title: 'We were wearing masks on the bus' - MacInnes backs health measures
articles.summary: Swimmer Keanna MacInnes believes the extra measures the Scottish and British teams have taken to ensure their competitors stay healthy has been a big factor...
articles.body:
Swimmer Keanna MacInnes believes the extra measures the Scottish and British teams have taken to ensure their competitors stay healthy has been a big factor behind her own breakthrough summer.

Her potential has been hampered by a combination of injury and illness in recent years.

She has had no such issues this time round, winning the first senior international medals of her career – three silvers and a bronze – at the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

That feat was bettered a few weeks later at last month's European championships in Paris where she won double gold.

And MacInnes, 25, told BBC Scotland: "These performances have probably been brewing over the past few years, I had a couple of disappointing summer meets just with injury and illness the past couple of years.

"I felt we have managed illness really successfully this year, the Scottish team and the British team, we were all wearing masks on the buses to and from the pool, which is something that not every team does.

"I am really grateful that our team has taken those steps and maybe some people are less prone to illness than others but everyone wants to help each other on that front so that is a big one."

Edinburgh's MacInnes is part of an exciting group of Scottish female swimmers that includes Katie Shanahan and Angharad Evans, who have also been racking up major medals over the past few months.

"Our squad training environment is just so positive right now, everyone is bouncing off each other, there has obviously been so much success, particularly with the girls at Stirling and I think we have definitely got loads of up-and-coming swimmers," MacInnes said.

"No one dragging their feet and being ready for retirement, everyone is fully committed to the LA cycle, so we all keep each other accountable and we are all just excited and happy to be there."

MacInnes made her Olympic debut in Paris two years ago and has got the Los Angeles 2028 Games very much in her sights.

"Maybe a decade ago people would have said that 25 was the end of a swimmers' career, especially a female swimmer," she explained.

"That view is definitely changing. Being funded by the UK lottery definitely helps people extend their career.

"There are so many things I can fix and improve and work on but I will need to sit down with my coach and decide what things we are targeting this year to drop time.

"It is everyone's dream to win an Olympic medal, there is a lot of data and stats saying that around 80% of the medals are made up from the top five from the worlds the year before so I guess short-term the target would be to be in that top five at the worlds this year."

articles.title: Steelers open season with familiar faces in new place
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH (BLACK AND GOLD NATION) — The Pittsburgh Steelers are opening their 2026 season at home against the Atlanta Falcons, the first time they have open...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH (BLACK AND GOLD NATION) — The Pittsburgh Steelers are opening their 2026 season at home against the Atlanta Falcons , the first time they have opened at home since 2023.

While the team has not played the Falcons since 2023, the Steelers will recognize some familiar faces donning the red and black. Atlanta had a full overhaul in the offseason, removing head coach Raheem Morris and releasing veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins .

Walking the sidelines for the Falcons is former Cleveland Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, who knows the Steelers all too well. In his time in Cleveland, Stefanski went 4-6 against Pittsburgh, with his lone playoff win coming against the Steelers in 2020.

While his location changed area codes, his philosophy remains the same.

"He's going to bring some things that we've seen in Cleveland twice a year," Steelers defensive lineman Keeanu Benton said. "But just being prepared for anything. I think we're doing a good job of getting a beat on what Atlanta did before he got there, and also what he did while he was with Cleveland."

Stefanski had to deal with quarterbacks Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders last season, which led them to a 5-12 record. Once hired in Atlanta, he had quarterback Michael Penix Jr. in his back pocket, but an injury made him find a backup plan.

That's where he landed on former Miami Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa , who was recently named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers. Having him under center gives him a chance to thrive with weapons such as running back Bijan Robinson , wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts .

The Steelers defense took note of the changes inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium and knows that it won't be a cakewalk.

"He got better playmakers now," Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen said. "I think he got guys that he get the ball into space and do a lot of damage with it. So it's going to be a heavyweight fight."

The last time Tagovailoa played the Steelers was in 2025 on a cold Monday night. The seven-year veteran threw two touchdowns and one interception in an offensive struggle against the Steelers' defense.

However, the fresh start in a new city can improve Tagovailoa's play drastically.

"It's a different offense, different system. I think the only thing you can prepare for is, like, quick timing. Just seeing how he does that," Queen added. "But at the same time, you know, they got new coaches, so it could mess with his technique or whatever it is. So, it's just really the first drive is coming out there and trying to figure everything out."

McCarthy acknowledged Stefanski's philosophy and playstyle when meeting with the media on Monday. He mentioned how he's focused on his team being prepared to meet the Falcons inside Acrisure Stadium in Week 1, a lesson he learned during his previous stints with the Dallas Cowboys and the Green Bay Packers .

"Today's work is really locking in how we need to play the game," McCarthy said. "It's the first game, and we're excited about the season opener and everything. I really don't care about the other team right now. We need to get our things set and get the direction clear of exactly how we want to play the game."

articles.title: 2026 College Football Watch Guide – Week 2
articles.summary: Conspiracies, blackouts, Hail Mary’s…week 1 had it all. How does week 2 stack up?
articles.body:
You could say it's true, the (Big) House always wins.

Week 1 had a little bit of everything for everybody. Huge blowouts? Yep . Nailbiter endings that came down to the wire? It had those too . Games played in semidarkness with no stadium clocks, PA system, or coach-QB communication? A little strange, but sure .

Speaking of stadium clocks, the one thing that resonated more than anything was the controversy surrounding the end of Western Michigan-Michigan game, where the Wolverines avoided a stunning upset after being granted a miracle second Hail Mary attempt after time expired.

Forget a last second victory, this was an extra second victory.

Initial reactions by most was rage as the NBC broadcast clearly showed the first pass clearly still in the air, untouched, with no time left on the clock. Conspiracy theories and conference favoritism accusations ran rampant. How could the replay booth get it so obviously wrong? The Big Ten must be tipping the scales in favor of one of their biggest brands. It also didn't help that it took them hours before releasing an official statement in ominous, pulp horror novel style, that did not address why NBC's clock, the point of truth for the rest of the country, was somehow wrong.

As I understand it, there was no "secret clock" only replay had access to. The stadium clock was the official time, on which replay and NBC had separate cameras trained on. The problem stems from the fact that replay and NBC were using different video feeds, and the NBC's was just slightly ahead the replay booth's. When replay used their feed, not the one millions at home saw, that's where the confusion and uproar started. FOX Sports Rules Analyst Mike Pereira explained the problem with this on The Joel Klatt Show on Monday.

Despite the leaps in technology used to sync broadcasts, replay, and stadium clocks to one single point of truth, variances as small as hundredths of a second can add up over the course of a game. If separate feeds have to be used, how do we stop this from happening again? Pereira's idea is good one. Another I've heard is using some sort of visual element in stadiums for when a clock expires, like the red lights surrounding the shot clock in basketball. On Wednesday, the Big Ten also announced that beginning this weekend it will be opening access to replay reviews , similar to what the ACC and Big XII already do.

All of these measures will be considered too little, too late for those who watched an apparent robbery in broad stadium light late Saturday evening.

Enough about clocks. Week 1 was as eventful as they come. Let's see what's up next in week 2.

Thursday, September 10 and Friday, September 11

The #23 Missouri @ Kansas Border War headlines the weeknight games. Both teams easily dispatched FCS opponents last week, each scoring 50+ to boot. But this game is obviously a step up for both programs and it could be closer than you might think. Rivalries are funny things, even ones that haven't been played to frequently recently.

It's a step up for the Scarlet Knights too, with Rutgers @ Boston College giving them an opportunity to flush an embarrassing week 1 loss to UMass. Rutgers QB Dylan Lonergan tossed three interceptions and the defense gave up 37 points to the Minutemen. Can he and the Scarlet Knights bounce back or are they bound for 0-2 in the young season?

#11 Oklahoma @ Michigan will be week 2's premier hate watch. Despite the Wolverines having absolutely no hand in the clock fiasco last week that won't stop America from still blaming them, and wanting to see them fall in more ways than just out of the AP poll. Bryce Underwood was underwhelming, going only 12/22 for a single TD and a pick against the Broncos. So disappointing was Underwood, Kyle Whittingham suggested that his days as the starter may be numbered if he doesn't improve. A tall task against the nation's #11 team.

#12 Alabama @ Kentucky gives the Wildcats their first opportunity to defeat the Tide in Lexington since 1997. QB Kenny Minchey tossed four touchdowns last week against Youngstown State. Normally an Alabama-Kentucky game wouldn't jump out, at the time of this writing Alabama is only favored by 10.5.

I'm also surprised by the line of Mississippi State @ Minnesota , where the Bulldogs are .5 point road favorites over the Gophers. MSU quarterback Kamario Taylor stood out in their opener, but I think Minnesota will be better than many think this year. Drake Lindsey is a solid QB, and running back Darius Taylor is a strong runner with 3 TDs of his own last week.

Of course Iowa State @ #21 Iowa makes the watch guide. Both teams dominated in their openers so we still don't have a solid picture of how they'll do against P4 competition. And damn it, we still don't know who'll be Iowa's longtime starter. Will one be decided Saturday night? Maybe finding out will be reason enough to tune in.

One game that doesn't need much excuse to draw your attention is #1 Ohio State @ #4 Texas . Both teams have national championship aspirations and the Buckeyes have won the last two meetings. Last year's meeting was an ugly 14-7 affair but one in which Ohio State always felt in control. It feels like Texas has to get over the Buckeye bump before they can break their title drought. This is the type of game you normally look forward to deep into the playoff bracket. It's a treat to get it in week 2.

articles.title: Former Sixers forward Robert Covington lands job with alma mater
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia 76ers forward Robert Covington lands a job with his alma mater at Tennessee State.
articles.body:
Robert Covington is a true champion of "The Process" era with the Philadelphia 76ers . An undrafted forward out of Tennessee State University and looking to earn his spot in the league after a season with the Houston Rockets , Covington then spent 4-plus seasons with the Sixers and earned that spot with hard work and a much-needed skillset.

Covington developed into one of the best 3-and-D players in the league. He was named to the All-Defensive First Team in 2017-18 and became a key piece for the Sixers in their turnaround. He carved out 11 years in the league with the Sixers, Rockets, Minnesota Timberwolves , Portland Trail Blazers , and Los Angeles Clippers .

As Covington transitions into his new chapter, he has earned a job with his alma mater as Chief Basketball Officer of Tennessee State's men's basketball program.

articles.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa leaves practice with an oblique injury
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa left practice Thursday with an oblique injury.  Tagovailoa bent over in obvious discomfort after throwing a pass d...
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. (AP) — Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa left practice Thursday with an oblique injury.

Tagovailoa bent over in obvious discomfort after throwing a pass during a portion of practice open to media and grabbed his right side. He dropped to the ground for a few seconds before getting up and trying to shake off the injury.

It's unclear if he returned to practice. The Falcons listed him as a limited participant.

Tagovailoa's first game with the Falcons is at Pittsburgh on Sunday. It's the same spot where he made the last start of his rocky final season with Miami .

Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski announced Monday that Tagovailoa will open the season as the starter and Michael Penix Jr. will be inactive. Cooper Rush will be the backup.

Penix did not play in a preseason game as he continues his recovery from a torn ligament in his left knee that ended his 2025 season.

Tagovailoa set a career high with 15 interceptions before he was benched for the final three games last season.

He had mixed results this preseason with Atlanta. He had two fumbled snaps in exhibition games, including one from the shotgun formation. He said ball security will be a key to returning to his form in 2023, when he led the NFL with 4,624 passing yards, and 2024, when he led the league by completing 72.9% of his passes.

articles.title: Elfyn Evans: Extra tyres essential to avoid WRC Rally Chile failures
articles.summary: The championship leader says the FIA’s increased allocation is the “bare minimum” needed for Chile’s abrasive gravel stages after the tyre problems seen in P...
articles.body:
World Rally Championship leader Elfyn Evans says the increased tyre allocation for Rally Chile is necessary to reduce the risk of failures on the abrasive gravel stages.

Ahead of the rally, the FIA confirmed that Rally1 crews will receive eight additional tyres for the event, increasing the allocation from 28 to 36 tyres. Crews will have a choice between a maximum of 16 soft and 28 hard Hankook tyres.

The regulation change is intended to reduce the risk of a repeat of the punctures and tyre delaminations that plagued Rally Paraguay last month. Hankook believes the failures were caused by a combination of long stage loops, unexpected high temperatures and rough conditions.

Chile's stages have previously served up a high puncture risk in the past, with the 2023 running of the event causing several tyre failures for then WRC tyre supplier Pirelli.

The increased allocation has largely been welcomed by drivers expecting another demanding weekend for tyre wear. Teams may also supply crews with up to two replacement tyres at a designated area in Arauco after the refuel zones, receiving the same number of used tyres in return.

"Chile always has a very varied stage type. Friday is quite fast but quite narrow and cambered roads, whereas Saturday is a bit wider and more flowing, but we also know tyre wear is a huge factor," said Toyota's Evans, who expects a difficult task opening the road as championship leader.

"I think realistically there was no way to make it through the day without those extra tyres so that was the bare minimum.

"I still believe Saturday will be tough for the tyres especially in the afternoon. I don't think it is straight-forward as being a flat out rally [with the extra tyres]."

Hyundai's Thierry Neuville, who like Evans was among those who suffered a tyre failure in Paraguay, added: "It is the same for everybody but it should slightly decrease the risk of delaminations which was an issue on some of the rougher gravel rallies and especially Paraguay.

"Here with long loops and some long stages to end the loop on Saturday afternoon, I think those added tyres are very welcome."

Despite the increase in tyre allocation, M-Sport-Ford's Josh McErlean believes a smart approach will be required to complete the rally without issue.

"I think we need them [the extra tyres]. From what we have seen in Paraguay with the delaminations and tyre wear, and we know from past year we have had delaminations here with other tyres, so I think come Saturday it will be quite the challenge to make it through the loop, so we have to be smart," said McErlean.

Interestingly, not all drivers are in favour of the extra rubber with Toyota's Oliver Solberg adding: "It helps the people who are not very good with tyre wear. I'm sad about it as normally I'm quite good with tyres. I would love to have not so many tyres, but that is how it is."

articles.title: Patriots news: Dave Portnoy could only laugh at NE announcer's reaction to Drake Maye's game-losing INT
articles.summary: The New England Patriots fanbase was not the happiest with how their team performed in their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, and the team shouldn...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots fanbase was not the happiest with how their team performed in their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, and the team shouldn't be happy either. With the game in their hands for most of the night, it was the fourth quarter that doomed them, and it revolved around Drake Maye , who threw three interceptions.

It was the last interception that happened to be the worst, and Patriots color analyst Scott Zolak had the call . After the interception, Zolak said, "No he didn't," and Dave Portnoy thought it was the funniest thing ever.

I just heard the call from Scott Zolak of the game ending INT. Made me laugh at least 'No he didnt' right up there with 'Do You Believe in Miracles!'" Portnoy wrote on X, formerly Twitter.

Though Portnoy had a laugh at the call, it was obvious that he wasn't pleased with his favorite team's performance.

"Only the 1st game of the season, but that was tough to watch," Portnoy said in a video . "Horrible game from Drake. That last throw, disgusting. We lose A.J. Brown with what I guess is going to be a pretty severe injury. The other guy, new guy, [Romeo] Doubs, just had a disgusting drop. Play calling sucked most of the night, I thought, on offense.

"The game was right there for the taking, obviously. It's only Week 1, but that was a s—-y way to start the season because they're a lot better than that. That was F-minus s–t."

Everyone was probably thinking what Portnoy was thinking at the moment, and the Patriots definitely have to play better if they want to get back to the team they were last season.

articles.title: Jaguars season opener: What fans need to know about stadium construction, traffic
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars kick off their 2026 NFL season at EverBank Stadium against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars kick off their 2026 NFL season at EverBank Stadium against the Cleveland Browns. The game will feature a reduced stadium seating capacity of 42,500 as construction continues on the venue's long-term renovation project.

The 27,000-seat reduction comes as the upper bowl, lower corners, Spa Deck, and Sky Patio are taken offline for the Stadium of the Future project, scheduled for completion in August 2028. The home opener will also serve as a 9/11 Remembrance game, with attendees asked to arrive early for commemorative programming and the national anthem.

Traffic exiting the stadium will be affected by ongoing construction on the Main Street Bridge, which limits southbound vehicles to a single lane. Westbound traffic leaving the stadium may be rerouted toward the Acosta Bridge to assist with traffic flow. Parking lots open 4 hours prior to kickoff and attendees must download mobile parking passes before arriving at assigned lots.

Renovations inside the stadium include new navigation options on the main concourse, which provides 360-degree circulation around the venue. Grand Staircases two and three in the North End join Grand Staircase one at Gate 1, alongside Ramps two and three and South End Zone escalators. Gate entry configurations have also been adjusted, with Gate two and the West Club gate merging into a single entry point, while the East Club gate remains restricted to Club and Suite ticket holders. Mobility assistance is available near each entry gate.

To handle warm temperatures, fans are permitted to bring two 16.9-ounce or smaller factory-sealed plastic water bottles into the stadium. Refillable water stations and complimentary cups are available at water fountains throughout the venue, alongside a Jacksonville Transportation Authority cooling bus located near Gate One. Guest Services booths are stationed at Sections 102, 123, 144, the Gallagher Club, and a new location near Ramp 3 at Section 130.

Pregame activities will take place at the Fan Entertainment Zone in the Flex Field behind Daily's Place, opening 3 hours prior to kickoff through Gates 1, 4, and seven. The first 300 fans visiting the area can receive a complimentary poster created by Jacksonville artist Mason Mushinski. The artwork features quarterback Trevor Lawrence holding a football and construction tools against the Jacksonville skyline. Additional pregame events include the Hard Rock Bet Party Bus on the West Plaza, autograph signings with former players, and youth football drills.

Construction on the Stadium of the Future project will continue throughout the 2026 and 2027 seasons ahead of the venue's completion in August 2028.

articles.title: Jerome Tang breaks silence on Kansas State firing: 'It still hurts'
articles.summary: Jerome Tang breaks his silence on Kansas State, saying his firing still hurts while reflecting on his return to Baylor.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — Former Kansas State basketball coach Jerome Tang made his first public comments about his former employer while speaking on Baylor 's in-house podcast.

Upon returning to Baylor as Scott Drew's associate head coach, Tang said on " The Sic 'Em Podcast " that he had an "unbelievable time in Manhattan, Kansas," while also complimenting the people, community and student body.

"We didn't win enough," Tang said. "That's the nature of the business, and they went in a different direction, but it didn't surprise God."

Tang was fired by Kansas State for cause midseason after his now-infamous postgame press conference following a loss to Cincinnati on Feb. 11. In the press conference, he described his players' efforts as "embarrassing" and continued, "These dudes do not deserve to wear this uniform, and there will be very few of them in it next year."

After he was fired four days later, Tang lawyered up to challenge the characterization of his termination in pursuit of his $18.675 million buyout. As of the afternoon of Sept. 10, Tang had yet to file a lawsuit in Riley County. It's believed his lawyers and Kansas State continue to meet behind closed doors to pursue a settlement.

Tang returned to Baylor on April 28, becoming the school's top assistant. He helped the Bears win a national championship in 2021. He was on Drew's staff from 2003-22.

During the podcast, Tang said he didn't sell his Waco, Texas, home and that his family was moving right in. He said he considered purchasing a home in Florida and taking a year off, but ultimately chose to continue coaching at the one place he would consider.

Kansas State and Baylor won't play in Manhattan this season. There's a chance the two could meet in the Players Era tournament in Las Vegas on Thanksgiving. They'll meet in Big 12 play in Waco on a date that has yet to be announced.

Tang was asked if he was still bitter toward the situation.

"I've learned that in dealing with grief and loss, there are some people that have suffered worse things than me, and I don't want to mix them," Tang said. "But there is some grief because you lose something that was important to you. I never went into any situation thinking about how it can help me get to the next place. That was always the place.

"Until God gave me a head job, there was no other place I wanted to be other than head coach at Kansas State, right? The only way God was going to get me to move was to rip me out of there. Sometimes your greatest strength, my loyalty, is also your greatest weakness, and God was nudging me and saying, 'Hey, you need to move,' and I would have thought that was the devil trying to take me off that mission.

"This was God's way of moving me. I understand that it still hurts. It still hurts. You lost something that was dear to you, something that you poured your whole heart and soul into and loved. I try to remember the good times. You go back and forth; some days it's OK, and then it goes to the other side where you think about the hurt. I love many people who are still there."

Tang was 71-57 as Kansas State's head coach. The Wildcats were 10-15 overall and 1-11 in Big 12 play when he was fired in mid-February.

The Wildcats have since hired former Belmont coach Casey Alexander and will enter the 2026-27 season with only one returning player. They tip off the season at home against South Dakota State on Nov. 3.

Wyatt D. Wheeler covers Kansas State athletics for the USA TODAY Network and Topeka Capital-Journal. You can follow him on X at @WyattWheeler_ , contact him at 417-371-6987 or email him at wwheeler@usatodayco.com

articles.title: Malik Nabers being coy about his availability for Sunday, but says it's his decision
articles.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said it is his decision whether he plays in the season opener on Sunday.
articles.body:
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said it is his decision whether he plays in the season opener on Sunday. However, he is not saying he will play.

He instead referred to John Harbaugh's comments from Wednesday, when the coach said he thinks Nabers is " ready to go , man."

" What Harbs said ," Nabers said, via video from SNY Giants.

Nabers is being coy despite a second consecutive full practice. He said it's still possible he might not play.

"That's a possibility. Like Harbs said, they're leaving the decision up with me," Nabers said, adding that it's his career.

Nabers tore his right ACL in a Sept. 28 game against the Chargers. He has previously said he will not come back on a snap count, and it seems like he's trending toward a full return for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

He caught nine passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 2 loss to the Cowboys last season.

"I grinded my ass off, excuse my language," Nabers said of his rehab. "I grinded, prayed hard, put in a consistent amount of work. Early, early mornings and late nights. I put in the work, and I did everything that I can to be in this position right now to be able to make the decision to play or to not play. If I am out there, I put in a great amount of work to know that I'm able to play, and I'm able to do exactly what I know I can do and will do."

The Giants' injury report remained the same as Wednesday, with defensive lineman Shelby Harris (Achilles), offensive lineman Bryan Hudson (knee), tight end Theo Johnson (shoulder) and offensive tackle Andrew Thomas (knee) remaining full participants.

articles.title: Falcons news: Is Cooper Rush going to start vs. Steelers amid Tagovailoa injury?
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons’ Week 1 quarterback situation might have just gone from complicated to disastrous. Cooper Rush told reporters Thursday that he took all o...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons ' Week 1 quarterback situation might have just gone from complicated to disastrous.

Cooper Rush told reporters Thursday that he took all of the first-team reps at practice after Tua Tagovailoa went down in pain, according to Marc Raimondi.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo provided even more concerning context .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"After Tua Tagovailoa went down in pain. The Falcons are prepping for the Steelers with QB3 right now," Garafolo reported.

That's not how Atlanta envisioned its final preparations for Week 1.

The Falcons announced Monday that Tagovailoa would start against Pittsburgh , with Rush serving as his backup. Michael Penix Jr., meanwhile, is expected to be inactive as Atlanta continues managing his recovery from last year's knee injury. Now Rush could suddenly be preparing to start the opener.

Nothing has been officially announced regarding Tagovailoa's availability, so taking all of the first-team reps doesn't guarantee Rush will be under center Sunday. But with only a few days remaining before kickoff, Atlanta clearly needs to have him prepared for that possibility. And Pittsburgh isn't exactly the opponent you'd choose for an emergency quarterback start.

Rush does at least provide the Falcons with an experienced option. The veteran has spent most of his career as a backup, including several seasons behind Dak Prescott in Dallas , and has been forced into starting situations before. Still, potentially entering Week 1 with your third option at quarterback is brutal.

Atlanta already knew Penix wasn't ready to play. If Tagovailoa's latest issue keeps him out as well, the Falcons' quarterback insurance policy will immediately be put to the test.

Week 1 hasn't even arrived yet, and Atlanta could already be scrambling.

articles.title: Phillies announce results on Brandon Marsh’s X-rays after 1-run loss to Astros
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies outfielder Brandon Marsh was unable to finish Thursday’s game against the Houston Astros due to injury.
articles.body:
Brandon Marsh gave the Philadelphia Phillies a scare Thursday when a foul ball forced him out of their series finale against the Houston Astros .

The Phillies later received some encouraging news on the outfielder. X-rays on Marsh's right foot were negative after he left the 2-1 loss in the ninth inning.

Marsh fouled a pitch from Astros reliever Bryan Abreu directly off his foot during his final plate appearance. He was shaken up by the hit and did not finish the game.

The Phillies initially diagnosed Marsh with a right foot contusion. Interim manager Don Mattingly said the negative X-ray results ruled out a more serious injury, but Marsh is dealing with significant soreness.

That soreness will keep him out of Philadelphia's starting lineup Friday. The Phillies can now hope Marsh needs only a short recovery after avoiding any structural damage.

The timing is important for Philadelphia. The Phillies are trying to keep pace with the Atlanta Braves in the NL East and will begin a three-game series in Atlanta after Thursday's loss.

Marsh went 0-for-3 with two strikeouts before leaving the game. He is hitting .267 with 17 home runs and 58 RBIs this season.

The outfielder has also struggled at the plate recently. That makes his availability even more important as Philadelphia enters the final stretch of the regular season.

Thursday's loss dropped the Phillies to 82-65. They now sit four games behind the Braves in the division.

The game itself was decided late. Zack Wheeler allowed one run over seven innings and struck out nine, but Philadelphia could not give him enough offense.

Cam Smith broke a 1-1 tie with a solo home run off Phillies closer Jhoan Duran in the ninth inning. The Astros held on to win the series two games to one.

For the Phillies, Marsh's negative X-rays provide some relief after an otherwise frustrating afternoon. The next step is seeing how quickly the soreness improves.

If Marsh returns soon, Philadelphia can move forward without another significant injury concern during an important stretch of the season.

articles.title: Pac-12 Power Rankings Heading Into Week 2
articles.summary: The Pac-12 had a rough opening week, going 2-6 against a challenging schedule that featured five games against ranked opponents, all on the road. While the c...
articles.body:
The Pac-12 had a rough opening week, going 2-6 against a challenging schedule that featured five games against ranked opponents, all on the road. While the conference struggled overall, several teams made significant moves in this week's power rankings.

Colorado State and Oregon State were the biggest risers, while Utah State suffered the biggest fall after an upset loss to Idaho State . With another challenging slate ahead, here are my Pac-12 power rankings heading into Week 2.

Boise State stays at No. 1 in this week's rankings after a narrow 34-27 road loss to a top-10 Oregon team. The Broncos looked the part of a top-25 team but could not pull off the big upset over Oregon. Boise State should come out of the game feeling like it can go 11-0 the rest of the year.

Looking ahead to this week, Boise State hosts Memphis in what will be a pivotal game for both schools' College Football Playoff hopes. Memphis is coming off a Week 0 win against UNLV in Las Vegas. The winner of this game will put itself in prime position for a CFP spot.

San Diego State is coming off a 53-20 win over FCS foe Portland State. The run game was very good against the Vikings, as SDSU had 237 yards on the ground. Questions still remain about quarterback play for the Aztecs this season.

The Aztecs will get their toughest test of their nonconference slate this week with a road game at the Rose Bowl against UCLA . The Bruins are coming off a 45-24 road win against Cal in Week 1 and should present a really good early-season test for SDSU.

The No. 3 spot stays with WSU this week after a 24-10 loss in the Apple Cup in Week 1. The WSU defense proved to be up for the challenge in Week 1 and projects as one of the better defenses in the Pac-12. However, the offensive side of the ball left more questions unanswered than answered after Week 1.

WSU has an away game against K-State in Week 2. This should be another good test for the Cougs against a K-State team that beat FCS Nicholls 71-3 in Week 1. I will be watching to see if the WSU offense looks improved and is able to open up the playbook a little bit more in Week 2.

Jim Mora and the Rams jumped up three spots to No. 4 this week after a 35-13 beatdown of rival Wyoming in Week 1. Coming into the season, there were questions about how good the quarterback play would be for the Rams this year. A lot of the questions were answered with Hauss Hejny throwing for five touchdowns and 214 yards.

Colorado State has a home game against Southern Utah this week before hosting No. 15 BYU in Week 3. If the Rams can take care of business this week, it would set up a massive matchup against BYU in Week 3.

After starting in last place in the offseason power rankings, Oregon State jumps all the way up to No. 5 after a solid Week 1 performance against Houston. The Beavers were able to keep it close against No. 22 Houston and gave themselves a chance to pull off an upset late in the fourth quarter. Quarterback Braden Atkinson looked the part of a top-end Pac-12 quarterback, throwing for 376 yards. If Atkinson can stay consistent, he will give Oregon State a chance to win any game on its schedule.

In Week 2, Oregon State gets the chance to host Texas Tech, which comes into the matchup ranked No. 13. The Beavers come in as heavy underdogs, but the first game of JaMarcus Shephard's tenure in Corvallis should have a good home environment. I will be watching to see if Atkinson can replicate his Week 1 performance and if the Beavers can keep the game competitive at home.

The Bulldogs drop two spots after a rough Week 1 performance against No. 14 USC that saw Fresno State shut out 39-0. Coming into the season, there were a lot of question marks around quarterback play and the offense. Week 1 did very little to address these concerns, and in fact, there are probably even more question marks around the Fresno State offense after Week 1.

Fresno State looks to get back on track this week with a home game against Sacramento State. This week should be a good test for the Fresno State offense. If the offense struggles to sustain drives and score points this week, it may be time to hit the panic button on the offense in Fresno.

Asking Texas State to beat a top-five Texas team on the road in Week 1 was always going to be a tough ask. However, I would have liked to see the Bobcats look a little bit more competitive in Week 1. The game ended 59-7, and Texas State struggled to move the ball on offense and did very little to stop the Texas offense.

G.J. Kinne's team will have to quickly flush the Week 1 result as the Bobcats have a huge rivalry game against UTSA this week. This feels like a game Texas State has to have to keep itself on track for a bowl game this year. I will be watching to see if the Texas State defense can hold up better against UTSA.

The Aggies fall all the way to the bottom of this week's power rankings after an embarrassing loss to FCS opponent Idaho State. Utah State moved the ball well but lost the turnover battle 4-0, plus had an additional three turnovers on fourth-down stops. The loss probably is not as bad for Utah State as it looks on the surface, but there is a lot of work for Bronco Mendenhall and his staff to get the program back on track.

Week 2 certainly does not get easier for the Aggies. Utah State will travel to No. 19 Washington, which is coming off a 24-10 Apple Cup win against WSU. Success for Utah State this week would be cleaning up the penalties and turnovers and keeping the game competitive against the Huskies.

articles.title: NYC stickball league keeps 9/11 hero’s legacy alive
articles.summary: THE BRONX (PIX11) — A legacy is kept alive and carried proudly through the Mercado family. On Stickball Blvd., the game lives on, played by children and fami...
articles.body:
THE BRONX (PIX11) -- A legacy is kept alive and carried proudly through the Mercado family. On Stickball Blvd., the game lives on, played by children and families across ages and generations.

The street variation of baseball known nationwide as stickball, on this one block in the Bronx, is known to the Mercado family as "our game."

It's also on that same strip of pavement where the New York Emperors Stickball League was founded 40 years ago, continuing a family tradition.

Born and raised in the Bronx, Steve Mercado, an FDNY 9/11 hero and former president of the NYESL, had a vision for the future. He wanted to bring stickball into city schools as a way to give children a safe outlet, especially those who couldn't afford to play baseball, a goal that now lives on through both of his sons.

Mercado was one of 11 firefighters from Engine 40, Ladder 35 in Manhattan who tragically lost their lives during the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks at the World Trade Center.

His oldest son, Skylar Mercado, was just six years old when he learned his world would change forever.

"I've learned to appreciate the thought process he had to go through, to do his duty and sacrifice his life trying to save as many people as he possibly could."

A brave act that shaped Skylar's own path.

Understanding the full weight of his father's sacrifice, he is now working to follow in his father's footsteps, hoping to join the FDNY while also helping carry the stickball league forward.

"I'm just trying to be half the man he was," Skylar said.

His father also hoped and dreamed stickball would become an Olympic sport, a dream Skylar now carries like a torch, the same passion alive since the league began in 1985.

In 2024, Skylar traveled to France to demonstrate stickball in front of Olympic officials.

"It was surreal, knowing what he wanted this to become and being able to do so in a European country. It was absolutely incredible."

Skylar says there are still many steps ahead, growing sponsorships, expanding outreach and helping the game reach a wider audience.

But the mission remains the same, keeping his father's and grandfather's legacy alive, and continuing to grow the game.

The NYESL will be running a Columbus Day Tournament on October 10 and 11 on Stickball Blvd. Entry fee is free for new teams, with eight players minimum.

To learn more about how to get involved, click here and here.

Nicole Alarcon is an award-winning digital content producer. She has covered local news for the tri-state area since 2021. She joined PIX11 News in 2026. See more of her work here .

articles.title: Former Titans' great Chris Johnson pens heartfelt letter to his family
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans legend Chris Johnson shares message to his family while preparing for his induction into the Ring of Honor.
articles.body:
As the reality of the heartbreaking news of Tennessee Titans ' legend Chris Johnson's ALS diagnosis continues to set in, a deep sadness can be felt across the NFL landscape, especially in Nashville, where Johnson made a lasting imprint on a community and an organization.

On Sunday, Tennessee will honor one of its all-time greats as it finally enshrine Johnson in the Titans' Ring of Honor, recognizing not only the player but the man, whose now well-documented battle with this devastating disease is something to behold.

This will be a significant weekend for Johnson, who is not only being celebrated by fans and the organization; he will also receive the "Champions Award" from the American Brain Foundation for his work spreading awareness of ALS.

Before kicking off this weekend, Johnson penned a letter to his children for The Players' Tribune and shared touching personal moments and insights from his career. But a few small lines in the letter captured the emotion and uncertainty perfectly.

How can a man just be perfectly healthy one day, running around with his kids in the yard, and then the next, your hand starts getting weak, and it just travels throughout your whole body until you can't talk anymore? Man, I've asked myself that question like a million times, and I still don't have an answer.

How can a man just be perfectly healthy one day, running around with his kids in the yard, and then the next, your hand starts getting weak, and it just travels throughout your whole body until you can't talk anymore?

Man, I've asked myself that question like a million times, and I still don't have an answer.

Unfortunately, for Johnson and others diagnosed with ALS, no one knows the answer, and we can only hope that one day doctors and scientists can find a cure for this devastating disease. Please take some time to read the heartfelt letter from Chris to his family, and cheer loudly when he receives the long-overdue honor of being enshrined in the Titans' Ring of Honor.

articles.title: The rumour Ben Shelton’s US Open rival Francis Tiafoe set him up with Trinity Rodman has already been addressed
articles.summary: Ben Shelton is set to meet Francis Tiafoe in the semifinal of the US Open to stand a chance at moving into his first career Grand Slam Final. His fellow Amer...
articles.body:
Ben Shelton is set to meet Francis Tiafoe in the semifinal of the US Open to stand a chance at moving into his first career Grand Slam Final. His fellow American has also previously claimed to have played a pivotal part in setting up Shelton with his soccer superstar girlfriend, Trinity Rodman.

Rodman and Shelton have been a power couple ever since they became public about their relationship in March 2025.

Both are constant features at each other's games and often copy each other's celebrations as well. Rodman even went the extra mile to be at Shelton's quarterfinal win against Carlos Alcaraz.

But according to Francis Tiafoe, all of this would not have happened without him.

Tiafoe is friends with Shelton, which is why it will be exciting to see how the semifinal between the two plays out.

Last year, the 28-year-old claimed that he played an important part in setting the couple up.

"By the way, I don't think people realize, I was like, the one who [connected them] — if we're going to be real," Tiafoe said, also comparing himself to CEO of Utah Jazz Danny Ainge.

He was also a little shocked at how Shelton decided to reveal to the world about his relationship with Rodman, who is a star in the US.

"I'm happy for him man. I was shocked he went up though… The elevator photo out the gate and then you don't go and tag [Rodman] and let everybody know who it is," he said.

"You don't need to go tag. Everybody knows who Trinity Rodman is. [The photo] at the end of the carousel, sick. That was tough."

Shelton has now cleared the air, confirming Tiafoe had no role to play in the two meeting.

"Tiafoe had nothing to do with it. He's taking credit, 'Oh, yeah, I put them together. I was like Danny Ainge.' He's a liar. He's trying to make it about himself. It's not about him, but that's funny."

Rodman also spoke about Tiafoe's claims.

"I can assure you Frances was not the reason we met or got together," Rodman said on SportsCenter. "I don't know why he's taking credit for that. Me and Ben can both cut that out. It was a solely me and Ben thing."

Shelton and Tiafoe will face off in the semis, the fifth time the two players have met in their careers. Shelton has three wins over Tiafoe and will be looking to add to that in front of a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium.

articles.title: Houston Astros beat Philadelphia Phillies behind Cristian Javier's strong start and Cam Smith's homer
articles.summary: Cristian Javier allowed one run in six innings and Cam Smith homered in the ninth as Houston beat the Phillies 2-1 to take the series.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA – In a game seeking separation, Cam Smith delivered.

Smith crushed a hanging splitter from Phillies closer Jhoan Duran for a tiebreaking home run in the ninth inning Thursday, lifting the Houston Astros to a 2-1 win and capping a positive series at Citizens Bank Park for both the second-year right fielder and his club.

The Astros took two of three from the Phillies, with Thursday's win ensuring they will take at least a two-game American League West lead into a series against the AL-best Tampa Bay Rays . Cristian Javier and three relievers combined to hold Philadelphia to three hits in the finale.

Smith homered in all three games of the series. The last was the most impactful. Duran left a first-pitch splitter over the plate with one out in the ninth. Smith hit it 421 feet for his 20th home run this season. Duran had not allowed a homer to a right-handed hitter on his splitter since 2024, per Statcast.

In a well-pitched game, the Astros had chances late. In the seventh, they loaded the bases with two outs on a single and two walks against Zack Wheeler . Phillies manager Don Mattingly left his starter in, at 105 pitches, to face pinch-hitter Yainer Diaz . On his 110th pitch, with a crowd of 37,100 standing, Wheeler got Diaz to whiff on a high sweeper, preserving a 1-1 tie.

An infield single and walk put two men on with no outs in the top of the eighth. Jeremy Peña broke from second on Isaac Paredes ' lineout to shortstop and was doubled off easily. It stung extra when Jose Altuve lined a two-out hit to the gap in left-center. Yordan Alvarez went first-to-third, appearing to turn his ankle as he arrived at third, but was stranded there.

Both starters were effective. Javier, making his 100th career start in the majors, had arguably his best of a rough season. Holding a potent Phillies offense to one run across six innings pared his ERA to 5.50. Javier scattered three hits and struck out five. He worked efficiently, totaling 79 pitches.

Wheeler outlasted him, working seven innings of one-run ball. The Astros took one at-bat with a runner in scoring position before the seventh. None of five on the afternoon yielded a hit. As it turned out, the decisive swing did not require one.

Javier had made one previous start in this ballpark, when he threw the first six innings of a combined no-hitter in Game 4 of the 2022 World Series. On Thursday, Javier worked with the same catcher, Christian Vázquez . He faced a Phillies lineup that featured five of the same hitters. He sported the same uniform combination – orange jersey, gray pants, dark blue long sleeves and socks.

He did not allow a hit for his first four innings. He faced the minimum in them. Kyle Schwarber worked a leadoff walk in the first. Javier retired his next 11 batters in a row, erasing Schwarber with a double-play grounder.

This is not the 2022 version of Javier. That pitcher threw 72% four-seamers in his World Series start. This one mixed in changeups and sweepers to a lineup with seven left-handed or switch-hitters. Few of those they put into play were hard-hit.

Luis Arraez led off the fifth and fell behind 0-2. Javier threw a four-seamer well above the zone. Arraez, a contact wizard, served it into left field for a single. Alec Bohm doubled to move him to third then made a mistake that quelled the inning. Bryson Stott 's grounder to shortstop scored Arraez, but Bohm broke on the ball in front of him and was thrown out. A double play ended the inning.

Javier returned for the sixth, for just the second time in 10 starts this season. An infield single and passed ball put the go-ahead run on second. The Astros let Javier face Schwarber, the majors' home run leader, and Trea Turner each a third time. Schwarber struck out swinging at a full-count fastball, Turner on a full-count changeup.

Wheeler was predictably tough. The veteran right-hander changed angles and speeds with a half-dozen pitches the Astros rarely squared up. Sixteen balls put into play against him averaged an 81.1 mph exit velocity. Wheeler generated 18 whiffs, struck out nine batters and walked two. Four of five hits against him were singles.

Christian Walker has enjoyed some success against Wheeler. The first baseman entered 9-for-21 against him in regular-season matchups, then singled softly in the second inning on a sinker that jammed him. Two batters later, Wheeler hung a curveball to Taylor Trammell , who yanked it into the right-field corner. Walker scored from first on the double.

Wheeler retired 12 of his next 13 batters. Six struck out. Cam Smith singled to begin the fifth; Wheeler erased him on a double play. The top of the Astros' lineup arrived for a third look in the sixth. Wheeler struck out Peña, Alvarez and Isaac Paredes, all swinging. Peña swung through a curveball and Alvarez and Paredes over splitters.

He escaped his seventh-inning jam on his 110th pitch, the second-most he has thrown in an outing this season. It punctuated his seventh start of at least seven innings with two or fewer runs allowed. Eight major-league pitchers entered Thursday with more this season, including his rotation-mate, Cristopher Sánchez. The Astros have totaled nine such starts.

The Astros will begin a three-game series Friday at Tropicana Field against the Tampa Bay Rays, who own the best record in the American League. Houston did not announce a starter for the series opener. Peter Lambert and Hayden Wesneski will start the final two games.

Houston took two of three from the Rays in a series at Daikin Park over July 4 weekend. The Rays began play Thursday with a four-game lead in the American League East.

"Their offense is pretty dynamic," said Astros manager Joe Espada. "They have guys in the middle of the lineup that can hit the ball out of the ballpark (and) that put the ball in play ... It's pretty well-rounded. They also can pitch, they throw a ton of strikes, it's a well-coached team. They've been doing things right there for a long time."

articles.title: Mural unveiled celebrating sporting greats Crocker and Best
articles.summary: The artwork replaced the long-standing George Best mural on Blythe Street in Sandy Row.
articles.body:
A mural has been unveiled in south Belfast to celebrate former IBF World Welterweight Champion Lewis Crocker.

The new artwork replaces the long-standing George Best mural on Blythe Street in Sandy Row and now features both sporting greats side by side.

The official unveiling took place on Thursday evening.

Lewis Crocker, who unveiled the mural, said it proved dreams can come true.

"I'm just a boy from Sandy Row and I'm beside George Best. Just to be up there and be recognised is amazing.

"It really is an unbelievable feeling. I could never imagine that as a kid."

DUP councillor Tracy Kelly, who helped organise the new mural, said that with a tribute to Alex Higgins also featured in the area, a dedication to Lewis was overdue.

"There have been talks and chats for months but we've finally got it here today.

"George has been on that wall for 20 years. He had to stay on the wall, I think if we had just taken him off people would have been too upset . I think it's a nice tribute to have both on the wall. "

Local businessman Ben Allen said it was always great to see something positive come to the Sandy Row area.

"Anything that's positive in Sandy Row has to be good. Lewis is the local celebrity . George Best is a massive pull for tourists so it's great to see the two of them on the same mural."

Jack Burke, who was one of those from the area who turned up to the unveiling, said: "Lewis is the toughest boxer ever so it's nice to be here."

Johnathan Johnston said the local community was buzzing for Lewis and the new mural.

"It's class to see Lewis on the wall. It is so well deserved. I always knew he was going to be a world champion."

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase eyeing Super Bowl, good health to begin Bengals season
articles.summary: There are now many signs pointing to Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase being full-go for the team's season-opener against Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
There are now many signs pointing to Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase being full-go for the team's season-opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . That's a good starting point for the latest Bengals player to indicate his only goals for the 2026 season are to win the Super Bowl.

Speaking during a Sept. 10 news conference at Paycor Stadium, Chase said he felt good and has taken on his normal workload in practice. Chase injured his knee during an Aug. 25 training camp practice when he collided with cornerback DJ Turner II.

The missed practices for Chase that followed the collision were precautionary, he said. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor said he anticipated both Chase and receiver Tee Higgins would be available for the Sept. 13 home opener, and Chase was listed in the Sept. 9-10 injury reports as a full participant in practice.

With health seemingly no longer threatening his ability to begin the season on time, Chase is set to begin his sixth NFL season with Super Bowl aspirations, but no personal or statistical aims he felt were worth mentioning during his Sept. 10 news conference.

"I don't have any personal goals this year," Chase said, "beside the Super Bowl and the AFC (championship). The other stuff is gonna come with that stuff."

Chase also begins 2026 as a team captain for the second year in a row. That task, Chase said, requires him to lead by example and with his words.

"The thing overall with being a captain is obviously, the whole team is looking at me," Chase said. "Everyone is really looking at me, asking me things and just expecting me to do the right thing. I always lead by example but I think it's just being more vocal."

articles.body:
The 2027 recruiting cycle still has a few months to go until the December signing period, but it feels like a majority of the top classes in the nation are set. Just two senior blue-chippers — according to the Rivals Industry Ranking — remain uncommitted, as of Sept. 8.

Things always move quick in the summer during official visit season, but this cycle has moved at a fervent pace since the beginning of the spring. While coaching changes, changes of heart and other factors will lead to some flips down the stretch, for the most part, top recruits look locked into their respective pledges.

Almost every ACC recruiting headline this cycle has revolved around Miami . The Hurricanes have the nation's No. 3 class — per the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings — and are the only ACC program to have a top-15 class with the season underway.

There are some new head coaches in the league who are making a splash in their new digs, while some old faces are still trying to show they've got their fastball. Rivals is taking a look at the updated ACC class rankings, now that football is finally back:

articles.body:
Santos has gained yet another "character" from Monica's Gang with the signing of forward Everton Cebolinha.

And Peixe's marketing team jumped on the "wave" by unveiling the player this Thursday (10).

Magali, one of the characters from the work created by Mauricio de Souza, was present at the event.

Her love of fish made Magali a Santos supporter, something the cartoonist and writer — now 90 years old — had already confirmed.

Check out below the "distinguished" presence at the presentation of Santos' new signing.

Mauricio de Souza revealed the preferences of the main characters from his greatest work in 1984, in a report by Placar magazine.

Magali was not yet a Santos supporter at the time, something that was revealed years later.

The only representative of Peixe was Pelezinho, who was created in honor of King Pelé in October 1976.

The teams supported by the other members of the main Monica's Gang cast are: Mônica (São Paulo), Cebolinha (Palmeiras), Cascão (Corinthians), and Chico Bento (São Bento).

Corinthians' connection with Cascão was reinforced last week with the official announcement of a partnership for a series of licensed products.
